    name: test-driven-development
    description: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix, before writing implementation code
    ---
    
    # Test-Driven Development (TDD)
    
    ## Overview
    
    Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.
    
    **Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.
    
    **Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**
    
    ## When to Use
    
    **Always:**
    - New features
    - Bug fixes
    - Refactoring
    - Behavior changes
    
    **Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
    - Throwaway prototypes
    - Generated code
    - Configuration files
    
    Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.
    
    ## The Iron Law
    
    ```
    NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
    ```
    
    Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.
    
    **No exceptions:**
    - Don't keep it as "reference"
    - Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
    - Don't look at it
    - Delete means delete
    
    Implement fresh from tests. Period.
    
    ## Red-Green-Refactor
    
    ```dot
    digraph tdd_cycle {
        rankdir=LR;
        red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
        verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
        green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
        verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
        refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
        next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];
    
        red -> verify_red;
        verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
        verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
        green -> verify_green;
        verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
        verify_green -> green [label="no"];
        refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
        verify_green -> next;
        next -> red;
    }
    ```
    
    ### RED - Write Failing Test
    
    Write one minimal test showing what should happen.
    
    <Good>
    ```typescript
    test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
      let attempts = 0;
      const operation = () => {
        attempts++;
        if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
        return 'success';
      };
    
      const result = await retryOperation(operation);
    
      expect(result).toBe('success');
      expect(attempts).toBe(3);
    });
    ```
    Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
    </Good>
    
    <Bad>
    ```typescript
    test('retry works', async () => {
      const mock = jest.fn()
        .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
        .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
        .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
      await retryOperation(mock);
      expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
    });
    ```
    Vague name, tests mock not code
    </Bad>
    
    **Requirements:**
    - One behavior
    - Clear name
    - Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)
    
    ### Verify RED - Watch It Fail
    
    **MANDATORY. Never skip.**
    
    ```bash
    npm test path/to/test.test.ts
    ```
    
    Confirm:
    - Test fails (not errors)
    - Failure message is expected
    - Fails because feature missing (not typos)
    
    **Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.
    
    **Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.
    
    ### GREEN - Minimal Code
    
    Write simplest code to pass the test.
    
    <Good>
    ```typescript
    async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
      for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        try {
          return await fn();
        } catch (e) {
          if (i === 2) throw e;
        }
      }
      throw new Error('unreachable');
    }
    ```
    Just enough to pass
    </Good>
    
    <Bad>
    ```typescript
    async function retryOperation<T>(
      fn: () => Promise<T>,
      options?: {
        maxRetries?: number;
        backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
        onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
      }
    ): Promise<T> {
      // YAGNI
    }
    ```
    Over-engineered
    </Bad>
    
    Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.
    
    ### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass
    
    **MANDATORY.**
    
    ```bash
    npm test path/to/test.test.ts
    ```
    
    Confirm:
    - Test passes
    - Other tests still pass
    - Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
    
    **Test fails?** Fix code, not test.
    
    **Other tests fail?** Fix now.
    
    **"Other tests" means the project's suite, not just your file.** A
    green run of the test you wrote is not a green suite. Before you call
    the change done, run the project's test command (bare `pytest`,
    `npm test`, `cargo test` — whatever the repo uses) even when your task
    named only one test file. A scope statement in your task bounds the
    deliverable, not your verification. Any failure that run shows —
    including one you didn't cause — goes in your report by name; a red
    test you watched scroll past and didn't mention is a report falsified
    by omission.
    
    ### REFACTOR - Clean Up
    
    After green only:
    - Remove duplication
    - Improve names
    - Extract helpers
    
    Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.
    
    ### Repeat
    
    Next failing test for next feature.
    
    ## Good Tests
    
    | Quality | Good | Bad |
    |---------|------|-----|
    | **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
    | **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
    | **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |
    
    When writing or changing any test, read [writing-good-tests.md](writing-good-tests.md) for the rules that keep tests honest:
    - Name the production change that would make the test fail — before writing it
    - Assert on real behavior, never on mock behavior
    - Keep test-only code in test utilities, out of production classes
    - Understand a dependency's side effects before mocking it
    
    ## Common Rationalizations
    
    | Excuse | Reality |
    |--------|---------|
    | "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
    | "I'll test after" | Tests written after pass immediately — which proves nothing. They may test the wrong thing, test the implementation instead of the behavior, or miss the edge case you forgot. You never watched it fail, so you never proved it can catch the bug. Test-first forces that failure. |
    | "Tests after achieve same goals (spirit not ritual)" | Tests-after answer "what does this do?"; tests-first answer "what should this do?" Tests written after are biased by the code you already wrote — you verify the cases you remembered, not the ones you'd have discovered. Coverage without proof the tests work. |
    | "Already manually tested" | Manual testing is ad-hoc: no record of what you covered, no way to re-run it when the code changes, easy to forget cases under pressure. "Worked when I tried it" ≠ comprehensive. Automated tests run the same way every time. |
    | "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy — that time is already spent either way. The real choice: rewrite with TDD (high confidence) vs. keep it and bolt tests on after (low confidence, likely bugs). Keeping code you can't trust is the waste. |
    | "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
    | "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
    | "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
    | "TDD will slow me down" | TDD IS the pragmatic path: catches bugs before commit, prevents regressions, lets you refactor without fear. "Pragmatic" shortcuts mean debugging in production — slower, not faster. |
    | "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
    | "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |
    
    ## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over
    
    - Code before test
    - Test after implementation
    - Test passes immediately
    - Can't explain why test failed
    - Tests added "later"
    - Rationalizing "just this once"
    - "I already manually tested it"
    - "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
    - "It's about spirit not ritual"
    - "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
    - "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
    - "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
    - "This is different because..."
    
    **All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**
    
    ## Example: Bug Fix
    
    **Bug:** Empty email accepted
    
    **RED**
    ```typescript
    test('rejects empty email', async () => {
      const result = await submitForm({ email: '' });
      expect(result.error).toBe('Email required');
    });
    ```
    
    **Verify RED**
    ```bash
    $ npm test
    FAIL: expected 'Email required', got undefined
    ```
    
    **GREEN**
    ```typescript
    function submitForm(data: FormData) {
      if (!data.email?.trim()) {
        return { error: 'Email required' };
      }
      // ...
    }
    ```
    
    **Verify GREEN**
    ```bash
    $ npm test
    PASS
    ```
    
    **REFACTOR**
    Extract validation for multiple fields if needed.
    
    ## Verification Checklist
    
    Before marking work complete:
    
    - [ ] Every new function/method has a test
    - [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing
    - [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)
    - [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test
    - [ ] All tests pass
    - [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
    - [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)
    - [ ] Edge cases and errors covered
    
    Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.
    
    ## When Stuck
    
    | Problem | Solution |
    |---------|----------|
    | Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |
    | Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |
    | Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |
    | Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |
    
    ## Debugging Integration
    
    Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.
    
    Never fix bugs without a test.
    
    ## Final Rule
    
    ```
    Production code → test exists and failed first
    Otherwise → not TDD
    ```
    
    No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

    description: >
      This skill should be used when working on web UI code (HTML, CSS, JavaScript,
      Tailwind, templates), when the user asks to "improve the dashboard", "fix the
      layout", "change colors", "redesign the web UI", "make it look better",
      "adjust styling", "update the CSS", "make it responsive", "fix the dark theme",
      "style the page", or any task involving visual web frontend changes. It enables

      user confirmation for each visual tweak.

    # Web UI Development with Visual Iteration
    
    ## Overview
    
    This skill enables pixel-accurate visual iteration on web UI changes. Instead of
    working blind, take browser screenshots after every change, evaluate them against
    the design system, and adjust autonomously. The result is faster, higher-quality
    frontend work without constant user review of cosmetic details.
    
    ## Prerequisites
    
    Before starting any web UI work:
    
    1. **Start the dev server** with hot-reload. Try in order:
       ```bash
       webui -r -v -p 3001                    # If webui CLI is installed
       koweb -r -v -p 3001                    # Legacy alias
       cd ~/scripts/modules/web_ui_tools && uvicorn web_ui_tools.app:create_app --reload --port 3001
       ```
       If none of these commands are available, ask the user how to start their
       development server and on which port.
    
    2. **Take a baseline screenshot** of the current state before making any changes.
       This enables before/after comparison.
    
    3. **Load Playwright tools** via ToolSearch for `playwright` to enable browser
       screenshot capabilities.
    
    ## Core Workflow: Edit-Screenshot-Evaluate Loop
    
    For every visual change (CSS, HTML, layout, color, spacing, typography):
    
    ### 1. Make the Change
    Edit the file (CSS, HTML, JS, template).
    
    ### 2. Take a Screenshot
    Navigate to the relevant page and capture:
    
    ```
    browser_navigate → http://localhost:3001
    browser_take_screenshot
    ```
    
    For specific views or states, navigate to the appropriate route first.
    
    ### 3. Evaluate Against Design System
    Compare the screenshot to the design system defined in
    `references/design-system.md`. Check:
    
    - Color usage matches the defined palette
    - Typography uses the correct font families and sizes
    - Spacing follows the 4px/8px grid
    - Metric cards follow the panel pattern
    - Layout respects the grid structure
    - Contrast ratios are sufficient for readability
    - Real-time data elements have appropriate update indicators
    
    ### 4. Adjust or Approve
    If the result does not match the design system or looks visually wrong:
    - Make the adjustment
    - Re-screenshot
    - Re-evaluate
    - Repeat until satisfactory
    
    If the result matches the design system and looks clean, move to the next change.
    
    **Do NOT ask the user for approval on individual visual tweaks.** The design
    system is the authority. Only escalate to the user when:
    - A design system rule conflicts with functionality
    - The change fundamentally alters the page layout or information hierarchy
    - Multiple valid approaches exist with meaningfully different aesthetics
    
    ## Screenshot Techniques
    
    ### Full Page Capture
    ```
    browser_navigate → target URL
    browser_take_screenshot
    ```
    
    ### Responsive Testing
    ```
    browser_resize → width: 1920, height: 1080  (desktop)
    browser_take_screenshot
    browser_resize → width: 1366, height: 768   (laptop)
    browser_take_screenshot
    browser_resize → width: 768, height: 1024   (tablet)
    browser_take_screenshot
    ```
    
    ### Component Isolation
    To evaluate a specific component, use the browser snapshot tool to identify
    the element, then evaluate its rendered appearance in the full screenshot.
    
    ### Dark Theme Verification
    The UI is dark-theme-only. Verify that:
    - Text is readable against dark backgrounds
    - Panel borders are subtle but visible
    - Active/hover states are distinguishable
    - Status colors pop against the dark canvas
    
    ## What "Good" Looks Like
    
    ### Metric Cards
    - Large numeric value (24-32px, bold, white)
    - Small label below (12px, muted gray)
    - Optional sparkline in top-right corner
    - Subtle border or background differentiation from canvas
    - Consistent padding (16px internal)
    
    ### Data Tables
    - Header row with muted text, no heavy borders
    - Alternating row backgrounds (subtle, 2-3% opacity difference)
    - Sortable columns indicated by caret icons
    - Monospace font for numeric data
    - Status badges with appropriate colors
    
    ### Live Feeds
    - Newest items at top
    - Timestamp in muted color
    - Event type badges with semantic colors
    - Smooth entry animation (fade-in or slide)
    - Auto-scroll with pause-on-hover
    
    ### Overall Layout
    - Fixed sidebar or top nav (not both)
    - Content area uses CSS Grid for panel arrangement
    - Panels have consistent border-radius (8px)
    - Spacing between panels: 16px gap
    - No horizontal scroll at 1366px+
    
    ## Additional Resources
    
    ### Reference Files
    
    Consult these for detailed specifications:
    
    - **`references/design-system.md`** - Complete color palette, typography scale,
      spacing system, component specifications, and CSS variable definitions
    - **`references/visual-qa-checklist.md`** - Step-by-step checklist to run after
      completing a visual change, covering accessibility, responsiveness, and polish
    
    ### Using the local-web Skill
    
    If Playwright MCP is unavailable, invoke the `local-web` skill as an
    alternative for accessing local development servers and taking screenshots.
    
    ## Anti-Patterns
    
    - **Working blind**: Never make more than 2-3 CSS changes without screenshotting
    - **Asking for color opinions**: The design system defines the palette; use it
    - **Ignoring contrast**: Always verify text readability on dark backgrounds
    - **Pixel-pushing without context**: Check the full page, not just the edited component
    - **Forgetting responsive**: Test at least desktop (1920) and laptop (1366) widths

    # Runmux Web UI — Phase 6 Agent Handoff: Advanced Workspace, Streams and History
    
    **Phase ID:** RUNMUX-WEB-P6
    **Status:** Candidate feature pool, **not** a single approved implementation assignment
    **Priority:** **P2–P3**; split into independently approved subprojects
    **Primary backlog:** I01–I08, T10–T11, N09–N14, H01–H11 advanced items, L12, C08–C12, W07–W11. T12 (interactive PTY attachment) is **already implemented** and is not a future feature.
    
    ## 1. Objective
    
    Build on the stable launcher, viewer, explorer, lifecycle and metrics foundation to make Runmux an efficient multi-process monitoring and management workspace. This phase intentionally contains multiple optional product areas. **Do not implement all of them as one PR.** First obtain user sign-off on concrete UX alternatives and verify source/backend support.
    
    ## 2. Candidate workstream A — Contextual process inspector
    
    **Provisional direction:** Keep the existing Details tab, then introduce a shared inspector that can function as an on-demand right drawer and a pinnable/resizable right panel. Candidate sections: Details, Events, Metrics, Files, Environment, Notes.
    
    - Inspector must not obscure essential process output by default.
    - Users may open/close it without navigating away from logs.
    - Pinning keeps it visible across run tabs, following the selected run.
    - Resize limits must protect minimum log workspace width.
    - Remember visibility and width as UI preferences, without storing sensitive process data.
    - A bottom-docked inspector is an **unresolved** design option. Do not construct a generalized docking platform without another decision.
    - Only show Events/Files/Environment views that have verified data access and authorization.
    
    ## 3. Candidate workstream B — Multiple output streams and split panes
    
    The approved long-term log interaction model includes:
    
    1. **Single:** One full-width log view.
    2. **Tabbed streams:** Choose among stdout, stderr, application log files or other **actual retained** sources; useful for 3+ streams.
    3. **Split panes:** Resizable simultaneous source views, typically stdout alongside stderr.
    
    Potential future keyboard interactions: `/` search, `n`/`N` matches, `f` follow, `p` pause *display*, and browser-safe shortcuts for pane switching and layout cycling. Do not rely on `Ctrl+W`, which commonly closes a browser tab.
    
    Before implementation, verify whether Runmux captures stdout and stderr separately and how per-stream retention works. A merged stream **cannot reliably be unmerged retroactively**. Each pane needs independent follow/scroll/search/filter state; output retrieval and rendering must remain bounded. Shared and per-pane state ownership should be defined before writing the UI.
    
    **Interactive PTY attachment already exists** through authenticated WebSockets and supervisor-managed input locking. This stream-layout work must preserve that contract. A *new* control-transfer or multi-user permission model would require its own threat model and approval; do not rebuild current PTY interaction.
    
    ## 4. Candidate workstream C — Events, history, and run discovery
    
    Enhance the existing historical-run explorer with a dedicated process overview or table **if volume justifies it**:
    
    - Sortable, filterable run list; active and historical records searchable without overloading the explorer.
    - Recent completions, failures, `LOST` explanations and restart history (where available).
    - Bounded output-history retrieval if persisted data exists; show retention/truncation explicitly.
    - Structured lifecycle events and an event timeline **only if event records exist or are deliberately introduced**.
    - Distinguish an inferred warning from a verified event. Avoid converting arbitrary log messages into authoritative run lifecycle events.
    - Date ranges, archived runs, and large-history pagination/virtualization where appropriate.
    - Optional warning/failure alerts, sampling-based thresholds and archival/retention policy controls require separate backend policy work and explicit approval.
    
    ## 5. Candidate workstream D — Workflow/productivity features
    
    Future optional features from the full concept:
    
    - Recent commands, saved process-launch presets and duplicate-into-launch form.
    - Pinned/reorderable tabs, searchable tab overflow and command palette.
    - Saved workspace layout/appearance settings; potentially adjustable dark/light theme and information density.
    - Task-oriented views for sessions, environment, files, storage, schedules, and notes—only where product usage and APIs justify dedicated navigation.
    - Advanced batch stop/restart/cleanup and unattended schedules, only after explicit authorization/confirmation models exist.
    
    Features shown in mockups such as New Process, Stop, Restart, resource charts and directories may belong to earlier phases. Do not duplicate them in this one.
    
    ## 6. Decision gates to settle before implementation
    
    | Decision | Current status | Required evidence/approval |
    |---|---|---|
    | Inspector on-demand + right pin | Preferred but provisional | UX sign-off; resizable design acceptance |
    | Bottom inspector docking | Open | Visual comparison and user approval |
    | Split vs tabbed stream switching | Direction approved | Actual independent output sources and API contract |
    | Browser PTY input | **Implemented** | Preserve existing WebSocket session/auth + supervisor attachment/input-lock contract; fix fidelity under Phase 2 |
    | Dedicated historical overview | Open | Run volume, search schema, desired columns |
    | Event/alert source | Unverified | Actual event model or approved event capture design |
    | Launch presets/templates | Future | Storage schema, secrecy, permission requirements |
    | Schedules/automation | Optional | Backend scheduling policy, scope and user approval |
    | Light theme | Open | Visual design approval and maintenance budget |
    
    ## 7. Suggested subprojects, not fixed implementation order
    
    - **6A — Inspector:** Right drawer + pin/resize, no arbitrary docking.
    - **6B — Multi-stream logs:** Stream tabs and resizable split panes, based on real sources.
    - **6C — History:** Dedicated run overview, bounded history browsing and real events.
    - **6D — Productivity:** Launch presets, keyboard command palette, workspace settings.
    - **No 6E PTY-control implementation:** Already delivered. Phase 2 may harden or correct terminal sizing/replay; any entirely new multi-user control-transfer policy requires a separate assignment.
    
    These may be assigned individually. Each must produce its own plan, tests and acceptance criteria once actual dependencies are known.
    
    ## 8. Common acceptance requirements
    
    Regardless of chosen subproject:
    
    - UI changes cannot mutate processes unintentionally, lose open runs or expose restricted command/environment content.
    - Long output and large historical registries must remain responsive through bounded retrieval/rendering.
    - Open tabs must be keyed by unique Run ID; log pane closing is view-only.
    - Resizing/docking should not corrupt terminal viewport geometry or ongoing process state.
    - Missing per-stream/history/telemetry data must be honestly described, not fabricated.
    - New write capabilities must use the verified authorized backend action model and be isolated in testing.
    - Visual and keyboard interaction must remain accessible and coherent at common desktop/ultrawide widths.
    
    ## 9. Agent handoff instruction
    
    > Treat **RUNMUX-WEB-P6** as a candidate roadmap, not blanket implementation authorization. First select **one** independently scoped subproject (6A–6D), inspect current source/API coverage and present unresolved UX/security decisions. Build only the approved slice, preserving Runmux registry and terminal semantics. Run validation with disposable registries and synthetic output. Return a concise PR/test report and recommend the next independent slice; do not create speculative navigation pages or backend services solely to mimic mockups.

    # Runmux Engineering Guide
    
    Last updated: 2026-06-22 06:44:27 -07:00
    
    This directory is the one-stop engineering introduction and handoff space for
    `runmux`. It explains what the program is, how it is built, its important
    terminal/process constraints, active implementation plans, and how LLM-driven work must
    be planned, verified, staged, approved, and resumed.
    
    Before working:
    
    1. Read applicable global and repository-level LLM instructions.
    2. Read [`HANDOFF.md`](HANDOFF.md) for exact current state and next action.
    3. Read [`plans/HANDOFF.md`](plans/HANDOFF.md) to find the latest active plan.
    4. Read that dated plan folder's `HANDOFF.md`, `STATUS.md`, `checklist.md`,
       implementation plan, and current stage plan.
    5. Inspect the source, tests, worktree, and recent commits.
    
    Information flows from general to specific:
    
    - Global/repository LLM instructions: generic workflow rules.
    - This README: runmux purpose, architecture, behavior, commands, and document
      map.
    - Root `HANDOFF.md`: immediate runmux worktree and resume state.
    - `plans/HANDOFF.md`: identifies the latest active or recently completed plan.
    - Dated plan folder: plan-specific requirements, checklist, status, and handoff.
    
    Optional project-wide future planning uses:
    
    - `plans/master_plan.md`: long-term future plan for runmux as a whole.
    - `plans/master_plan_checklist.md`: tracks completion of entire dated
      folder-level implementation plans.
    
    These files are currently optional and need not exist. Detailed stages and
    features remain inside their dated plan folders.
    
    Do not select a plan from its folder timestamp alone. Confirm the candidate from
    `plans/HANDOFF.md` using its status/checklist, file timestamps, the staged
    worktree, and recent commits limited to `modules/runmux/`.
    
    ## Project Overview
    
    `runmux` is a cross-platform terminal process manager and multiplexer. It starts
    programs under detached supervisor processes, records shared metadata, preserves
    ANSI terminal output, and lets independent PowerShell or Unix shell sessions
    list, view, interact with, monitor, restart, duplicate, pause, kill, and remove
    managed runs.
    
    The user-facing goal is similar to the program-management portion of tmux:
    
    - A managed program continues after the launching shell detaches.
    - Any later shell can discover it through `runmux ls` or `runmux list`.
    - Multiple terminals can view the same output.
    - Interactive terminal programs run through a PTY/ConPTY where available.
    - Run metadata and command history survive individual shell sessions.
    - Full-screen and in-place-rendered programs retain ANSI color and cursor
      behavior as faithfully as the host terminal permits.
    
    Runmux is especially intended for long-running Python CLIs and TUIs such as
    `ytaedl`, `video-dedupe`, and `file-util ls`.
    
    ## Current Capabilities
    
    - `runmux run PROGRAM ...` starts a supervised program and normally attaches
      interactively.
    - `-D/--detach` starts and returns to the shell.
    - `-w/--view` or `-a/--attach` starts in view-only mode.
    - `runmux list` provides a live selectable list.
    - `runmux ls` prints a one-shot list.
    - `runmux view -i ID` follows ANSI output without forwarding ordinary keys.
    - `runmux interact -i ID` follows output and forwards program input.
    - `runmux kill`, `restart`, `duplicate`, `pause`, `resume`, `rm`, and
      `remove-finished` manage lifecycle.
    - `runmux stats` shows live process-tree resource information.
    - `runmux history`, `save`, and `cmd` provide command history and saved commands.
    - Numeric IDs start at zero and removed IDs are reused.
    - Working directory and terminal dimensions default to the launching shell.
    - Detached Windows supervisors and children are created without visible blank
      console windows.
    
    ## Architecture
    
    ### CLI
    
    `src/runmux/cli.py` owns argparse definitions and top-level command handlers.
    The `runmux` entry point is `runmux.cli:main`.
    
    ### Registry
    
    `src/runmux/store.py` owns the SQLite registry. The normal state directory is:
    
    - Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\runmux`
    - Unix-like systems: `$XDG_STATE_HOME/runmux` or `~/.local/state/runmux`
    - Tests or isolated commands: `--state-dir PATH`
    
    The registry uses WAL mode and stores runs, process identifiers, supervisor IPC
    ports, terminal dimensions, status, timing, commands, and attachment sessions.
    
    ### Supervisor
    
    Each managed run has a detached `python -m runmux.supervisor` process. It:
    
    - Launches the child under ConPTY/pywinpty on Windows when available.
    - Uses a PTY on Unix-like systems.
    - Falls back to pipe capture when Windows PTY startup fails.
    - Pumps child output into a byte-preserving `output.ansi` file.
    - Exposes authenticated localhost TCP IPC.
    - Owns process input, resize, status, kill, pause, and resume operations.
    
    The supervisor must remain alive for interaction. Closing or killing the
    supervisor makes the managed run unavailable even if stale registry data exists.
    
    ### Clients
    
    `src/runmux/client.py` implements list, view, and interact behavior.
    
    - Output clients tail the shared ANSI log.
    - Interact clients open an authenticated input socket.
    - Ctrl-X is the runmux command prefix in interact mode.
    - View and interact attachments have unique session IDs and heartbeat leases.
    - The supervisor, not a client, is authoritative for input ownership.
    
    ### History
    
    The current implementation stores history and saved commands under
    `modules/runmux/.runmux/commands.json`. The active implementation plan will migrate this to
    locked JSONL history, separate saved commands, configuration, retention, search,
    and summaries.
    
    ## Terminal and Process Intricacies
    
    Runmux deals with terminal byte streams, not logical UI widgets. Important
    constraints:
    
    - ANSI output may be split across arbitrary read chunks.
    - Full-screen TUIs emit cursor movement, screen clears, alternate-screen
      switches, scroll regions, terminal queries, and in-place redraws.
    - Logs must remain raw; runmux-specific status UI must only affect attached
      clients.
    - Windows special keys arrive through `msvcrt` and must be translated to ANSI
      sequences before forwarding.
    - Enter is a carriage return on Windows.
    - Terminal dimensions must be sent to the managed PTY.
    - Client exit paths must restore cursor visibility and terminal modes.
    - Heartbeat leases recover from abruptly closed terminal windows.
    - Multiple interact clients require supervisor-controlled serialization; client
      assumptions are insufficient.
    - `Ctrl+Shift+X` is not portable because terminals generally encode it the same
      as `Ctrl+X`.
    - The browser Terminal fits xterm.js to the visible panel, but the supervised
      PTY keeps its startup dimensions while the browser attachment is read-only.
      The browser sends resize requests only while that attachment holds the input
      lock; a TUI can therefore wrap or clip when its PTY size differs from the
      browser viewport.
    
    ## Active Implementation Plan

    The prior multi-attach and input-lock implementation plan remains the source
    history for supervisor ownership behavior.
    
    This is the implementation plan for one set of features. It is not the
    ultimate end goal or complete permanent roadmap for runmux.

    2. Multi-attach and FIFO input ownership: implemented, committed, and manually approved.
    3. Attachment status UI and persistent settings: partially implemented;

    4. History search, replay, interactive/fzf selection, and summaries: detailed

    Immediate plan status is in

    Feature-level state and stage completion times are in

    ## Planning Documents
    
    Each implementation plan too large for one safe cycle gets a dated folder:
    
    ```text
    docs/plans/YYYYMMDD-HHMM_<descriptive-plan-name>/
    ```
    
    It contains:
    
    - `00_implementation-plan.md`: complete intended result of this feature set.
    - Numbered stage plans: ordered implementation/commit boundaries.
    - `STATUS.md`: current operational state.
    - `HANDOFF.md`: implementation-plan-specific resume guidance.
    - `checklist.md`: stage completion ledger and feature implementation/test state.
    
    Each dated implementation plan uses a branch named from the plan followed by its
    creation timestamp. It is merged only after the user validates the completed
    program and approves the merge.
    
    Every `docs/` directory and planning subdirectory contains a `HANDOFF.md`.
    It may link to more authoritative documents, but it must tell an unfamiliar LLM
    what the folder contains, what is current, and what to read next.
    
    Master plans and stage plans end with a local-time `Last edited` timestamp.
    
    Canonical repository plans also live under `plans/modules/runmux/` because that
    is required by `MODULE_STANDARDS.md`.
    
    ## Cycle Workflow
    
    1. Plan the stage.
    2. Populate the stage section in the active plan folder's `checklist.md`.
    3. Implement features individually.
    4. Mark each feature implemented but not fully tested immediately after coding.
    5. Run the previously passing suite.
    6. Add focused tests.
    7. Run old and new tests together.
    8. Promote the stage to implemented and tested.
    9. Run Ruff, Black check, compileall, coverage, and smoke checks.
    10. Review and document the diff.
    11. Stage, but do not commit.
    12. Stop for user manual testing.
    13. Commit only after explicit approval.
    14. Begin the next stage only after the approved commit.
    
    The user may explicitly authorize continuous stage execution. That skips the
    pause between stages, but not stage planning, tests, documentation, or commits.
    
    The proposed generic rules being reviewed for global adoption are available in
    [`GLOBAL_LLM_DOCUMENTATION_INSTRUCTIONS.md`](GLOBAL_LLM_DOCUMENTATION_INSTRUCTIONS.md).
    
    ## Verification Commands
    
    From the repository root:
    
    ```powershell
    pytest --tb=short -q .\modules\runmux\
    ruff check modules\runmux modules\scripts_help\scripts_help\registry\registry.py
    black --check --line-length 120 modules\runmux
    python -m compileall -q modules\runmux\src\runmux
    pytest --cov=runmux --cov-report=term-missing -q .\modules\runmux\
    ```
    
    Use module-local state for smoke tests:
    
    ```powershell
    runmux --state-dir modules\runmux\.pytest_tmp_root\smoke run --detach -- python -c "import time; time.sleep(30)"
    runmux --state-dir modules\runmux\.pytest_tmp_root\smoke ls
    runmux --state-dir modules\runmux\.pytest_tmp_root\smoke interact -i 0
    ```
    
    ## Documentation Responsibilities
    
    - Update this README somewhat at every cycle close.
    - Update it comprehensively when a full implementation plan is completed or the
      architecture/public behavior changes materially.
    - Update `HANDOFF.md` whenever current work, known risks, staged state, or next
      action changes.
    - Update the active plan's `STATUS.md` and `checklist.md` throughout
      implementation.
    - Keep global/repository LLM instructions stable and generalized;
      project-specific live details belong in `HANDOFF.md`.
    - Do not force incoming LLMs to reconstruct intent exclusively from source code.
    
    The desired handoff is that the user can tell a new LLM only: read the
    repository instructions and the runmux docs, inspect the worktree, and continue.

    function deferred() {
      let resolve;
      const promise = new Promise((done) => { resolve = done; });
      return { promise, resolve };
    }
    
    function element(tagName = "div") {
      const listeners = new Map();
      const classes = new Set();
      return {
        tagName,
        children: [],
        attributes: {},
        dataset: {},
        hidden: false,
        _textContent: undefined,
        get textContent() {
          if (this._textContent !== undefined) return this._textContent;
          if (this.children.length > 0) {
            return this.children.map((c) => (typeof c === "string" ? c : c.textContent || "")).join("");
          }
          return "";
        },
        set textContent(val) {
          this._textContent = val;
          this.children = [];
        },
        value: "",
        checked: true,
        get className() {
          return [...classes].join(" ");
        },
        set className(val) {
          classes.clear();
          if (val) val.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean).forEach((c) => classes.add(c));
        },
        scrollHeight: 0,
        scrollTop: 0,
        clientHeight: 0,
        style: {},
        lastElementChild: { textContent: "" },
        classList: {
          add(...cs) { cs.forEach((c) => classes.add(c)); },
          remove(...cs) { cs.forEach((c) => classes.delete(c)); },
          toggle(c, force) {
            if (force === undefined) {
              if (classes.has(c)) { classes.delete(c); return false; }
              classes.add(c); return true;
            }
            if (force) { classes.add(c); return true; }
            classes.delete(c); return false;
          },
          contains(c) { return classes.has(c); },
        },
        addEventListener(name, handler) { listeners.set(name, handler); },
        dispatch(name, ...args) { listeners.get(name)?.(...args); },
        setAttribute(name, value) {
          this.attributes[name] = String(value);
          if (name === "class") this.className = `${value}`;
        },
        getAttribute(name) { return this.attributes[name] ?? null; },
        append(...children) { this._textContent = undefined; this.children.push(...children); },
        appendChild(child) { this._textContent = undefined; this.children.push(child); },
        replaceChildren(...children) { this._textContent = undefined; this.children = [...children]; },
        focus() {},
        blur() {},
        select() {},
        scrollIntoView() {},
        closest() { return null; },
        click() { this.dispatch("click"); },
      };
    }

    import json
    import sqlite3
    import sys
    import time
    from pathlib import Path
    
    import pytest
    
    from runmux.store import RunNotFoundError, RunStore
    from runmux.telemetry_store import TelemetryStore
    from runmux.web import create_runmux_web_app
    from runmux.web_adapter import ReadOnlyRunmux
    
    
    def _insert_run(
        store: RunStore,
        run_id: str,
        *,
        created_at: str,
        status: str = "finished",
        name: str | None = "sample",
        started_at: str | None = None,
        ended_at: str | None = None,
        exit_code: int | None = 0,
        restart_of: str | None = None,
        duplicate_of: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        with sqlite3.connect(store.db_path) as connection:
            connection.execute(
                """INSERT INTO runs (
                    id, numeric_id, name, status, created_at, updated_at, started_at, ended_at,
                    exit_code, pid, supervisor_pid, program, argv_json, cwd, env_overrides_json,
                    port, auth_token, log_path, command_line, restart_of, duplicate_of, rows, columns
                ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, NULL, NULL, ?, ?, ?, ?, NULL, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 24, 80)""",
                (
                    run_id,
                    int(run_id[-6:], 16),
                    name,
                    status,
                    created_at,
                    created_at,
                    started_at,
                    ended_at,
                    exit_code,
                    sys.executable,
                    "[]",
                    str(store.state_dir),
                    "{}",
                    "test-token",
                    str(store.state_dir / "secret-output.log"),
                    "secret command arguments",
                    restart_of,
                    duplicate_of,
                ),
            )
    
    
    def _record(store: RunStore, index: int) -> str:
        run_id = f"20261024-120000-{index:06x}"
        _insert_run(store, run_id, created_at="2026-10-24T12:00:00+00:00")
        return run_id
    
    
    def test_query_runs_keyset_is_stable_and_rejects_changed_filters(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        store = RunStore(tmp_path)
        created = "2026-10-24T12:00:00+00:00"
        ids = [f"20261024-120000-{index:06x}" for index in range(5)]
        for run_id in ids:
            _insert_run(store, run_id, created_at=created)
    
        first = store.query_runs(limit=2)
        assert [item.id for item in first.items] == sorted(ids, reverse=True)[:2]
        assert first.has_more is True
    
        _insert_run(store, "20261024-130000-000099", created_at="2026-10-24T13:00:00+00:00")
        second = store.query_runs(limit=2, cursor=first.next_cursor)
        assert [item.id for item in second.items] == sorted(ids, reverse=True)[2:4]
        assert second.has_more is True
    
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="filters do not match"):
            store.query_runs(limit=2, cursor=first.next_cursor, status="failed")
    
    
    def test_query_runs_filters_are_applied_in_sql_and_run_ids_remain_identity(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        store = RunStore(tmp_path)
        created = "2026-10-24T12:00:00+00:00"
        _insert_run(
            store, "20261024-120000-000001", created_at=created, ended_at=created, name="Same", status="failed", exit_code=2
        )

        event_cursor = first_event_page["next_cursor"]

        while event_cursor:
            next_event_page = backend.get_run_events(run_id, limit=2, cursor=event_cursor)
            all_event_pages.extend(next_event_page["events"])
            event_cursor = next_event_page["next_cursor"]
        assert {event["event_type"] for event in all_event_pages} >= {"pause", "resume", "checkpoint"}

    async function testLifecyclePauseAndResumeExecution() {
      const { context, getElement, requests } = dashboardHarness();
      const db = context.__dashboard;
    
      const runningRun = { ...run("20261024-051200-abcdef", "active worker"), status: "running" };
      const pausedRun = { ...run("20261024-051202-654321", "paused worker"), status: "paused" };
    
      db.setRuns([runningRun, pausedRun]);
    
      // 1. Supported platform: execute pause on running run
      db.setSystemCapabilities({ platform: "linux", supports_pause_resume: true });
      db.setSelectedId(runningRun.id);
      db.updateLifecycleControls(runningRun);
    
      context.fetch = async (url, options) => {
        requests.push({ url, options });
        if (url.includes("/api/runs/20261024-051200-abcdef/pause")) {
          return response({ action: "pause", status: "ok", message: "Process paused successfully." }, 200);
        }
        if (url.includes("/api/runs/20261024-051202-654321/resume")) {
          return response({ action: "resume", status: "ok", message: "Process resumed successfully." }, 200);
        }
        if (url.includes("/api/runs")) {
          return response([runningRun, pausedRun], 200);
        }
        return response({});
      };
    
      const pauseBtn = getElement("#action-pause-btn");
      assert.equal(pauseBtn.textContent, "Pause");
      pauseBtn.click();
      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 20));
    
      const pauseReq = requests.find((r) => r.url.includes("/pause"));
      assert.ok(pauseReq, "Pause request should have been dispatched");
    
      const feedbackBanner = getElement("#lifecycle-feedback");
      assert.equal(feedbackBanner.hidden, false);
      assert.match(feedbackBanner.textContent, /paused successfully/i);
    
      // 2. Supported platform: execute resume on paused run
      db.setSelectedId(pausedRun.id);
      db.updateLifecycleControls(pausedRun);
      assert.equal(pauseBtn.textContent, "Resume");
      pauseBtn.click();
      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 20));
    
      const resumeReq = requests.find((r) => r.url.includes("/resume"));
      assert.ok(resumeReq, "Resume request should have been dispatched");
      assert.match(feedbackBanner.textContent, /resumed successfully/i);
    
      // 3. Unsupported Windows platform: directly calling executeLifecycleAction shows 501 error banner
      db.setSystemCapabilities({ platform: "win32", supports_pause_resume: false });
      context.fetch = async (url, options) => {
        requests.push({ url, options });
        return response({ detail: "Pausing processes is not supported on Windows." }, 501);
      };
    
      await db.executeLifecycleAction("pause", runningRun.id);
      assert.equal(feedbackBanner.className, "lifecycle-feedback feedback-error");
      assert.match(feedbackBanner.textContent, /not supported on Windows/i);
    }

    # Handoff - Runmux Phase 6C: Historical Run Discovery & Events Backend
    
    **Branch:** `codex/runmux-historical-runs-backend-20261024`
    **Worktree:** `.worktrees/runmux-historical-runs-backend`
    **Base Commit:** `8befeae3375740e21cdfe17a081387f0e3cf8f54`
    **Assignment:** Phase 6C Historical Run Discovery, Filtering, Keyset Pagination, and Lifecycle Events Backend.
    
    ---
    
    ## 1. Operating Boundaries & Invariants
    
    - **Strict File Ownership:** Python backend only (`store.py`, `models.py`, `web_adapter.py`, `web.py`, test files). Do NOT touch frontend files (`dashboard.js`, `dashboard.css`, `index.html`) or Phase 5C charts (owned by Agent B).
    - **Read-Only Invariant:** Historical discovery must never mutate the registry or restart/terminate managed processes.
    - **Contract Preservation:** Existing `GET /api/runs` remains an unchanged `list[dict[str, Any]]`. Dedicated `GET /api/runs/history` provides bounded filtering and keyset pagination.
    - **Privacy Allowlist:** Redact process arguments (`argv_json`), paths (`cwd`, `log_path`), environment variables (`env_overrides_json`), and credentials (`auth_token`, `port`).
    - **Provenance Truthfulness:** Explicitly differentiate recorded events (`"telemetry_store"`) from authoritative registry transitions (`"registry_record"`). Never present an inferred state transition as a recorded event.
    
    ---
    
    ## 2. Delivered API Contract
    
    | Endpoint | Response | Bounds / behavior |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `GET /api/runs` | Existing array of allowlisted run objects | Preserved unchanged for current consumers |
    | `GET /api/runs/history` | `{items, next_cursor, has_more, page_size, total_count, sort_by, sort_dir, filters}` | `limit` defaults to 50, capped at 200; SQL filters; optional exact `total_count` with `include_total=true` |
    | `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/events` | `{run_id, events, next_cursor, has_more}` | `limit` defaults to 200, capped at 1,000; chronological keyset pages combine recorded telemetry and timestamped registry markers with explicit provenance |
    | `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/lineage` | `{run_id, root_run_id, ancestors, descendants, total_restarts, total_duplicates, truncated}` | `limit` defaults to 200, capped at 1,000 |
    
    History filters include status lists, active/terminal state, case-insensitive exact or substring name search, inclusive timezone-aware `since`/`until` bounds for `created_at`/`started_at`/`ended_at`, exit code, failed/lost state, restart/duplicate parent IDs, and restart existence.
    
    The cursor binds the sort, direction, and normalized filters. Ordering uses the selected value and immutable Run ID as a unique tie-breaker. A first-page `(created_at, id)` watermark excludes runs with a later creation timestamp; a same-second insertion with a lower Run ID may still appear. Pages read current state independently, so a run whose status changes may enter or leave a filtered result set; the API does not hold a database snapshot across requests. A SQLite VM-step budget bounds query work. Exact counts are opt-in because they can scan all matching rows.
    
    Event objects expose event type, timestamp, provenance, optional telemetry event ID, linked Run ID, and registry status/exit code. Free-text reason and arbitrary telemetry details are omitted. Registry transitions are labeled `registry_record`; persisted telemetry rows are labeled `telemetry_store`. No new event capture or retention behavior was added.
    
    ## 3. Verification and Limitations
    
    - Focused tests: `python -m pytest tests/historical_runs_api_test.py tests/store_test.py tests/web_adapter_test.py -q -s` — 28 passed.
    - Synthetic 10,000-run registry: first page 19.26 ms, next keyset page 14.54 ms, status/name-filtered page 3.22 ms (latest recorded run; Windows, local disposable SQLite).
    - Lint: `python -m ruff check src/runmux/store.py src/runmux/models.py src/runmux/web_adapter.py src/runmux/web.py tests/historical_runs_api_test.py` — passed.
    - Compile: `python -m compileall -q src/runmux/store.py src/runmux/models.py src/runmux/web_adapter.py src/runmux/web.py` — passed.

    - [x] Request process history in Dashboard and Expanded modes; request host history only in Expanded. Minimal and Inline issue no history requests.

    # Status - Runmux Phase 6C: Historical Run Discovery & Events Backend
    
    **Date:** 2026-10-24
    **Branch:** `codex/runmux-historical-runs-backend-20261024`
    **Base:** `origin/main` (`8befeae3375740e21cdfe17a081387f0e3cf8f54`)
    **Current Stage:** Complete (backend-only)
    **Approval State:** Implemented, verified, and pushed; not merged.
    **Implementation Commit:** `7c7360935242c6ed42bc3ac54040934b67520161`
    
    ---
    
    ### Progress & Operational Ledger
    
    1. **Worktree & Isolation Established:**
       - Dedicated worktree `.worktrees/runmux-historical-runs-backend` created from `origin/main`.
       - Feature branch `codex/runmux-historical-runs-backend-20261024` active.
       - Verified native Windows environment. Disposable test state only.
    
    2. **Architecture Research & Matrix Complete:**
       - Evaluated 3 distinct data categories: Run History (`registry.sqlite3`), Metric History (`telemetry.sqlite3`), and Lifecycle Events (`telemetry_events` / `runs` transitions).
       - Produced `01_existing_capabilities_matrix.md` and `00_implementation-plan.md`.
    
    3. **Completed implementation:**
       - Added indexed SQL-side filters and stable keyset pagination with a 1–200 page bound, opaque filter-bound cursors, and an initial-created-time watermark. Later pages exclude runs with a creation timestamp later than the first-page watermark; a same-second insertion with a lower Run ID may still appear. Status changes are reflected per request and can move a record into or out of a filter; this is not a database snapshot.
       - Added a SQLite VM-step budget for history and lineage queries. Exact `total_count` is optional (`include_total=true`) because counting can require a full filtered scan.
       - Added bounded restart/duplicate lineage, allowlisted history serialization, recorded telemetry-event access with chronological keyset cursors, and registry timestamp markers with explicit provenance.
       - Added authenticated `GET /api/runs/history`, `/api/runs/{run_id}/events`, and `/api/runs/{run_id}/lineage`. Existing `GET /api/runs` remains an array response.
       - No frontend, telemetry collection, retention policy, or event-capture changes were made.
    
    4. **Validation:**
       - `python -m pytest tests/historical_runs_api_test.py tests/store_test.py tests/web_adapter_test.py -q -s`: 28 passed; 10,000 synthetic run registry benchmark most recently measured first page 19.26 ms, next page 14.54 ms, and status/name-filtered page 3.22 ms.
       - `python -m ruff check src/runmux/store.py src/runmux/models.py src/runmux/web_adapter.py src/runmux/web.py tests/historical_runs_api_test.py`: passed.
       - `python -m compileall -q src/runmux/store.py src/runmux/models.py src/runmux/web_adapter.py src/runmux/web.py`: passed.
       - The ordinary `python -m runmux --version` resolves the environment's already-installed 0.13.0 package. The feature branch updates module metadata to 0.14.0; verify the local source with `PYTHONPATH=src python -m runmux --version`.
       - Direct HTTP TestClient execution was not completed: Windows asyncio loop initialization blocked in the sandbox while creating its internal socket pair. Adapter behavior and route registration were tested; HTTP auth is inherited from the existing authenticated `/api` router and existing auth middleware.
    
    5. **Remaining limitations:**
       - The registry stores current lifecycle state, not a transition log. Registry events therefore represent only recorded timestamps and explicit relationship fields; telemetry events are separately tagged `telemetry_store`.
       - Telemetry event free-text reasons and arbitrary details are withheld because their payloads have no safe disclosure allowlist.
       - Lineage page totals count direct restart/duplicate relationships for the selected run; returned ancestor/descendant nodes are capped and indicate truncation.
       - The legacy duplicate roadmap at `modules/runmux/docs/RUNMUX_WEB_UI_MASTER_ROADMAP.md` is older than the revised canonical handoff roadmap. Both trackers were updated to show this branch as complete but unmerged.
    # Checklist - Runmux Phase 6C Historical Run Discovery & Events Backend
    
    **Branch:** `codex/runmux-historical-runs-backend-20261024`
    **Base Commit:** `8befeae3375740e21cdfe17a081387f0e3cf8f54`
    **Status:** Complete (Backend only; branch remains unmerged)
    
    ---
    
    ## 1. Inspection & Architecture
    
    - [x] Inspect persistent process registry (`store.py`, `models.py`)
    - [x] Inspect existing history/list/detail APIs (`web.py`, `web_adapter.py`)
    - [x] Differentiate 3 data categories: Run History, Metric History, Lifecycle Events
    - [x] Produce existing capabilities matrix (`01_existing_capabilities_matrix.md`)
    - [x] Formulate keyset pagination and filtering architecture (`00_implementation-plan.md`)
    
    ---
    
    ## 2. Storage Layer & Pagination Engine (`store.py`, `models.py`)
    
    - [x] Add secondary composite indexes in `RunStore.migrate_db()`:
      - `(created_at, id)`
      - `(status, created_at, id)`
      - `(ended_at, id)`
      - `(name, created_at, id)`
      - `(restart_of)`
      - `(duplicate_of)`
    - [x] Implement cursor serialization/deserialization (URL-safe base64 JSON)
    - [x] Implement `RunStore.query_runs()` with keyset pagination:
      - Stable sort order by `created_at`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `name`, `numeric_id`
      - Global `id` tie-breaker
      - Deterministic behavior when records are added or mutated during pagination
      - Bounded page sizes (`limit`: 1 to 200, default 50)
      - Return `items`, `next_cursor`, `has_more`, `total_count`
    - [x] Implement multi-attribute filtering:
      - `status`, `state` (active/terminal)
      - `name` (exact / substring)
      - `since` / `until` with `time_field` selection
      - `exit_code`, `failed_only`, `lost_only`
      - `restart_of`, `duplicate_of`, `has_restarts`
    - [x] Implement `RunStore.get_run_lineage()` (ancestor and descendant chains)

    ## 3. Web Adapter & Serialization (`web_adapter.py`)
    
    - [x] Implement `ReadOnlyRunmux.query_runs_history()`
    - [x] Implement `ReadOnlyRunmux.get_run_events()`:
      - Query discrete `telemetry_events` from `telemetry.sqlite3`
      - Bound chronological results with a keyset cursor
      - Extract structured lifecycle transitions from `runs` record

    ## Implementation Notes
    
    - Query pages use SQL filters, stable `(sort_value, Run ID)` ordering, a created-time watermark, page limits of 1–200, and a bounded SQLite VM instruction budget. A new same-second record with a lower Run ID can still fall within the watermark.
    - `total_count` is nullable unless `include_total=true`; exact counts can scan the matching records.
    - Status changes between requests are reflected in each page, so a record may move into or out of a filtered result set. The cursor prevents offset row shifts; it does not create a multi-request SQLite snapshot.
    - API route execution could not be exercised through TestClient in this Windows sandbox because asyncio loop initialization stalled while creating its internal socket pair. Adapter tests and route registration passed.

    ## Limitations

    # Implementation Plan - Runmux Phase 6C: Historical Run Discovery & Events Backend
    
    **Date:** 2026-10-24
    **Branch:** `codex/runmux-historical-runs-backend-20261024`
    **Prerequisite:** Phase 5C integrated into `origin/main` at `8befeae3375740e21cdfe17a081387f0e3cf8f54`
    **Status:** In Progress (Backend-only workstream)
    
    ---
    
    ## 1. Goal & Architectural Boundaries
    
    Deliver a high-performance, bounded, and authenticated backend API for historical run discovery, filtering, cursor pagination, and lifecycle-event querying without altering existing process supervision or breaking existing frontend process-list API contracts.
    
    ### Strict File Ownership & Boundaries
    - **Backend-Only Scope:** Python modules in `modules/runmux/src/runmux/` (`store.py`, `web_adapter.py`, `web.py`, `models.py`) and dedicated unit/integration tests in `modules/runmux/tests/`.
    - **Frontend Protection:** Zero modifications to `dashboard.js`, `dashboard.css`, or `index.html`. (Agent B owns Phase 5C frontend charts and Phase 6 frontend integration).
    - **Read-Only Invariant:** Historical run queries and event lookups must remain strictly read-only; they must never mutate the registry or restart/terminate processes.
    - **Privacy & Security:** All run metadata outputs must pass through strict serialization allowlisting, omitting process arguments (`argv_json`), working directories (`cwd`), environment variables (`env_overrides_json`), and IPC credentials (`auth_token`, `port`).
    
    ---
    
    ## 2. Technical Design & Capabilities
    
    ### A. Indexing & Schema Upgrades (`registry.sqlite3`)
    In `RunStore.migrate_db()`, introduce secondary composite indexes:
    1. `idx_runs_created_at_id`: `(created_at, id)` for default reverse-chronological and forward pagination.
    2. `idx_runs_status_created_at`: `(status, created_at, id)` for lifecycle state filtering (e.g. `failed`, `lost`, `running`).
    3. `idx_runs_ended_at_id`: `(ended_at, id)` for filtering recent completions and failures.
    4. `idx_runs_name_created_at`: `(name, created_at, id)` for name searches and duplicate process name resolution.
    5. `idx_runs_restart_of`: `(restart_of)` for forward lineage queries.
    6. `idx_runs_duplicate_of`: `(duplicate_of)` for duplicate tree queries.
    
    ### B. Keyset (Cursor) Pagination Engine
    - **Cursor Structure:** Opaque URL-safe base64-encoded JSON containing `(sort_column, sort_value, run_id, sort_direction)`.
    - **Deterministic Tie-Breaking:** `runs.id` is globally unique and immutable (22 characters). It acts as the final tie-breaker for all sort orders.
    - **Query Structure:**
      ```sql
      WHERE (status IN (...))
        AND (created_at < :cursor_val OR (created_at = :cursor_val AND id < :cursor_id))
      ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC
      LIMIT :page_size + 1
      ```
    - **Guarantees:**
      - No `OFFSET` scans: page traversal seeks after the last `(sort_value, id)` key.
      - A first-page `(created_at, id)` watermark excludes runs with a later creation timestamp. A same-second new run with a lower Run ID can still appear after the cursor.
      - Pages read current state independently; a status update may move a record into or out of a filtered result set. This is not a multi-request database snapshot.
      - A SQLite VM-step budget bounds pathological filter work; callers can narrow filters after a budget error.
      - Explicit bounded page sizes: default 50, maximum 200 items per response.
      - Bounded response memory: fetch at most `limit + 1` records; exact total counts are opt-in because they can scan all matches.
      - Invalid cursor handling: returns HTTP 400 with actionable validation detail.
    
    ### C. Rich Filtering Capabilities
    - `status`: Single status or comma-separated list (`running,failed,killed`).
    - `state`: Macro filter (`active` = pending/running/paused; `terminal` = finished/failed/killed/lost).
    - `name`: Case-insensitive substring match or exact match.
    - `since` / `until`: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp or Unix epoch float.
    - `time_field`: Target field for time filtering (`created_at`, `started_at`, `ended_at`).
    - `exit_code`: Specific exit code integer.
    - `failed_only`: Boolean flag matching `status = 'failed'` or `(status = 'finished' AND exit_code != 0)`.
    - `lost_only`: Boolean flag matching `status = 'lost'`.
    - `restart_of` / `duplicate_of`: Exact parent run ID.
    - `has_restarts`: Boolean flag finding parent runs that have been restarted.
    
    ### D. Genuine Lifecycle Events & Provenance
    Expose `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/events` combining:
    1. **Recorded Events (`provenance: "telemetry_store"`):** Discrete events recorded in `telemetry_events` table (e.g. pause, resume, worker recovery, checkpoint events), returned in bounded chronological cursor pages.
    2. **Registry Markers (`provenance: "registry_record"`):** Structured timestamps and relationships from `runs` table:
       - `registered` at `created_at`
       - `started` at `started_at`
       - `terminated` at `ended_at` with `exit_code`, `status`
       - `restarted_from` / `restarted_by` with linked Run IDs
       - `duplicated_from` / `duplicated_by` with linked Run IDs
    3. **Explicit Distinction:** Every event object has a `provenance` field (`"telemetry_store"`, `"registry_record"`). The registry is not an event log; missing transitions are not reconstructed. Free-text reasons and arbitrary event details are withheld without a safe schema.
    
    ### E. Endpoints & API Contracts
    1. `GET /api/runs/history`:
       - Paginated historical discovery endpoint returning items, cursor, page metadata, and active filters.
    2. `GET /api/runs`:
       - Existing browser process-list endpoint. Retains 100% backward compatibility (returns the existing `list[dict[str, Any]]`).
    3. `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/events`:
       - Returns chronological list of genuine lifecycle events and registry state transitions with explicit provenance.
    4. `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/lineage`:
       - Returns full ancestor and descendant tree of restarts and duplicates.
    
    ---
    
    ## 3. Staged Implementation Plan
    
    - **Stage 1: Storage Layer & Pagination Engine (`store.py`, `models.py`)**
      - Add indexes in `migrate_db`.
      - Implement `query_runs_keyset` with cursor generation, validation, dynamic filtering, and stable tie-breaking.
      - Implement lineage traversal methods (`get_run_lineage`).
    - **Stage 2: Web Adapter Integration (`web_adapter.py`)**
      - Add `ReadOnlyRunmux.query_runs_history()` and `ReadOnlyRunmux.get_run_events()`.
      - Implement secure allowlist serialization and provenance tagging.
    - **Stage 3: Authenticated Web Endpoints (`web.py`)**
      - Expose `GET /api/runs/history`, `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/events`, `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/lineage`.
      - Maintain backward compatibility for `GET /api/runs`.
      - Add session authentication and validation error handlers.
    - **Stage 4: Comprehensive Test Battery & Benchmarking**
      - Unit tests for cursor encoding/decoding, boundary handling, concurrent additions, collision tie-breaking.
      - Scalability benchmark with 10,000 synthetic runs; report first-page, next-page, and filtered-query latency.
    - **Stage 5: Documentation & Integration Readiness**
      - Update roadmap, `STATUS.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, `checklist.md`.
      - Verify all combined backend tests.
    # Phase 6C: Existing Capabilities & Architecture Matrix
    
    **Date:** 2026-10-24
    **Workstream:** Runmux Phase 6C (Historical Run Discovery & Events Backend)
    **Baseline Commit:** `8befeae3375740e21cdfe17a081387f0e3cf8f54` (Phase 5C integrated into `main`)
    
    ---
    
    ## 1. Three Core Data Categories
    
    Before implementing historical run discovery and events, Runmux explicitly distinguishes three fundamentally different categories of historical data:
    
    | Category | Definition | Source of Truth | Storage Engine | Retention & Lifecycle | Primary Identification |
    | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
    | **1. Run History** | Persistent records of processes ever managed (pending, running, finished, failed, killed, lost). | `registry.sqlite3` (`runs` table) | SQLite (WAL mode) | Permanent until explicitly pruned (`prune_terminal_runs`, `clean`) | Immutable Run ID (`YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-xxxxxx`) & recycled `numeric_id` |
    | **2. Metric History** | Periodic time-series resource measurements (CPU, RSS, I/O, threads, GPU) sampled while `runmux web` is running. | `telemetry.sqlite3` (`telemetry_*` tables) | SQLite (WAL mode, incremental auto-vacuum) | Multi-tier: 1h raw, 24h 1-minute rollup, 7d 5-minute rollup (50 MB target budget) | Partitioned by `(run_id, timestamp)` |
    | **3. Lifecycle Events** | Discrete state transitions and supervisor operations with verified event provenance. | `telemetry.sqlite3` (`telemetry_events` table) & `runs` timestamp deltas | SQLite (`telemetry_events`) & structured registry attributes | 7-day retention in telemetry store; permanent state markers in registry | `(run_id, timestamp, event_type)` |
    
    > [!IMPORTANT]
    > **Metric samples do not establish authoritative lifecycle events.** While gaps in periodic metric samples indicate process pauses or supervisor restarts, authoritative lifecycle events must have genuine provenance (supervisor operation records or verified state transitions). Inferred state changes must never masquerade as recorded events.
    
    ---
    
    ## 2. Existing Capabilities Matrix
    
    | Functional Area | Current Capability in Codebase | Limitations & Gaps | Target in Phase 6C |
    | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
    | **Run Record Storage** | Stores 24 structured attributes in `registry.sqlite3` (`runs` table) including `created_at`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `exit_code`, `pid`, `restart_of`, `duplicate_of`. | No secondary indexes on `status`, `created_at`, `ended_at`, `name`, `restart_of`, or `duplicate_of`. Queries scan table sequentially. | Add targeted indexes via `migrate_db` to support $O(\log N)$ historical queries. |
    | **Process Listing (`GET /api/runs`)** | Returns an unbounded array of all runs in registry ordered by active status then `created_at DESC`. | Non-deterministic ordering when `created_at` collisions occur (no tie-breaker). Memory consumption scales linearly with registry size. | Preserve existing contract for `GET /api/runs` (unbounded array), add optional pagination params, and introduce `GET /api/runs/history`. |
    | **Pagination** | None. `RunStore.list_runs` accepts only an integer `limit`. | Offset pagination (`LIMIT/OFFSET`) causes row skipping/duplication when runs are added or state changes. Unbounded scans. | Implement deterministic keyset (cursor) pagination using `(sort_value, id)` with base64url opaque cursors. |
    | **Filtering** | `RunStore.list_runs` supports only `statuses: list[str]`. | No filtering by time range (`since`/`until`), name, exit code, recent failures, lost runs, or restart/duplicate relationships. | Support multi-attribute filtering: `status`, `state` (active/terminal), `since`/`until`, `name`, `exit_code`, `failed_only`, `lost_only`, `restart_of`. |
    | **Sorting** | Hardcoded: `CASE WHEN status IN ('pending', 'running', 'paused') THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, created_at DESC`. | Cannot sort by `started_at`, `ended_at`, `name`, or `numeric_id`. Inconsistent ordering on timestamp collisions. | Support sorting by `created_at`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `name`, `numeric_id` with `id` tie-breaker. |
    | **Lifecycle Events** | `telemetry_store.py` provides `telemetry_events` table (`event_id`, `run_id`, `timestamp`, `event_type`, `reason`, `details_json`). | Only queried within `/api/runs/{id}/telemetry/history` window. No standalone endpoint for process lifecycle events. | Provide dedicated `GET /api/runs/{id}/events` combining recorded telemetry events and structured registry transitions with explicit provenance. |
    | **Lineage & Relationships** | `runs` table records `restart_of` and `duplicate_of` Run IDs. `web_adapter.py` walks `restart_of` backward for telemetry charts. | Forward traversal (who restarted this run?) requires full scan. No dedicated relationship API. | Provide relationship mapping and forward/backward lineage resolution with cycle detection. |
    | **Security & Privacy** | `serialize_run` allowlists safe fields, redacting `argv_json`, `cwd`, `env_overrides_json`, `auth_token`, `port`. | Must guarantee new history search and discovery endpoints do not leak redacted environment variables, arguments, or tokens. | Re-use strict allowlist serialization across all new historical query and event responses. |
    
    ## 3. Phase 6C Implementation Outcome
    
    - `GET /api/runs` remains the existing array response. New historical browsing is isolated in `GET /api/runs/history` and uses SQL filters, keyset cursors, deterministic Run ID tie-breaking, a first-page creation watermark, a 1–200 item limit, and a SQLite VM-step budget.
    - Queryable sort keys are `created_at`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `name`, and `numeric_id`. Time bounds are inclusive and normalized to UTC second precision. Exact counts are opt-in because they may scan every matching row.
    - A page reads current registry state when requested. The cursor avoids offset shifting and excludes runs with a later creation timestamp; a same-second new run with a lower Run ID may still appear. Status updates can change membership between pages. This is not a cross-request database snapshot.
    - `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/events` returns chronological cursor pages of at most 1,000 entries. Recorded telemetry rows are labeled `telemetry_store`; timestamp markers and stored restart/duplicate links are labeled `registry_record`. No transition is inferred from metric samples. Free-text reason and arbitrary event details are withheld.
    - `GET /api/runs/{run_id}/lineage` traverses explicit restart and duplicate Run IDs in both directions. The response caps each path at the requested limit, sets `truncated`, and reports direct relationship counts for the requested run.
    - New adapters use read-only SQLite connections. History items and lineage nodes use allowlists. The API routes are attached to the existing authenticated `/api` router.
    - The 10,000-record disposable registry benchmark is in `tests/historical_runs_api_test.py`; latest recorded timings are in the Phase 6C status report.

    # Runmux Phase 6C Historical Explorer Frontend
    
    **Date:** 2026-10-24  
    **Branch:** `codex/runmux-6c-history-frontend-local-pilot-20261024`  
    **Worktree:** `.worktrees/runmux-6c-history-frontend-local-pilot`  
    **Baseline:** `4591b3247bdfafe82f0b8d1a73f40002152a6c2b`  
    **Scope:** Browser implementation of Phase 6C historical run discovery, lifecycle event presentation, and explicit restart/duplicate lineage.
    
    ## Goal and boundaries
    
    Add a bounded, paginated History workspace view using the existing authenticated Phase 6C endpoints. Preserve the current process explorer, process tabs, Output, Terminal, Details, lifecycle controls, and Phase 5C charts. Keep Run ID as the only run identity. Do not change API contracts, backend behavior, telemetry retention, event persistence, supervisor behavior, or other Phase 6 slices.
    
    The browser must not disclose arguments, working directories, environment data, or credentials. Closing the History view or a process tab remains view-only. Persisted telemetry events and registry-derived timestamp markers must be visibly labeled by provenance; missing events or relationships remain explicitly empty/unavailable.
    
    ## Approaches considered
    
    1. **Add filters to the live process explorer.** This would reuse its location, but risks replacing or overloading the active-run workflow and cannot cleanly represent cursor pages plus historical event/lineage detail.
    2. **Open a modal history browser.** This would avoid changing workspace tabs, but gives a large table, filter controls, pagination, and event detail too little space and creates nested navigation.
    3. **Add a dedicated History workspace tab (selected).** It preserves the process explorer and existing run tabs, provides adequate room for filters and a bounded table, and can open any row into the existing immutable Run ID view. The existing Details area will host per-run events and explicit lineage navigation.
    
    ## Data and interaction contract
    
    - Query only `GET /api/runs/history`; default to 50 items and keep every response bounded. Use cursor history for Previous/Next navigation; never load the entire registry. Do not request exact totals by default.
    - Use only API-supported filters and sort keys: status/state, name, inclusive `since`/`until` with `time_field`, exit code, failed/lost, restart/duplicate parent, and restart existence; sort by `created_at`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `name`, or `numeric_id` with supported direction.
    - Reset cursors on filter/sort changes. Abort or disregard stale requests when filters, page, selected Run ID, or workspace change. Render at most one server page (maximum 200) plus bounded event/lineage views.
    - Opening a row selects/opens the existing run view using its full immutable Run ID. Duplicate names never share state. The History workspace tab and per-run tabs are view-only.
    - Fetch `/api/runs/{run_id}/events` and `/lineage` only for the selected run's Details view. Label `telemetry_store` as recorded telemetry and `registry_record` as a registry timestamp/relationship marker. No inferred lifecycle events. Navigate only by explicit relationship Run IDs.
    - Use text nodes/textContent for server values. The backend allowlist is the source for safe fields; never render private command arguments, cwd, environment, or secrets.
    - Preserve the established dark IDE styling and responsive behavior. Do not modify Phase 5C chart semantics or address issue #11.
    
    ## Stages and acceptance
    
    1. **Contract and plan:** verify endpoint parameters, cursor/filter binding, authentication inheritance, event provenance, lineage IDs, privacy allowlist, and Phase 5C integration. (Complete.)

    function renderWorkspaceTabs() {
      const tabs = $("#workspace-tabs");
      const previousScrollLeft = Number(tabs.scrollLeft) || 0;
      tabs.replaceChildren();
      const openedRuns = openRunIds.map((runId) => runs.find((run) => run.id === runId)).filter(Boolean);
      let scrollTargetElement = null;
      tabs.hidden = false;
      for (const run of openedRuns) {
        const tab = document.createElement("div");
        tab.className = `workspace-tab${run.id === selectedId ? " active" : ""}`;
        const activate = document.createElement("button");
        activate.type = "button";
        activate.className = "workspace-tab-select";
        activate.setAttribute("role", "tab");
        activate.setAttribute("aria-selected", `${run.id === selectedId}`);
        const displayName = run.name || run.command || "Unnamed process";
        activate.title = `${displayName} · ${run.id}`;
        activate.setAttribute("aria-label", `Open ${displayName}, run ${run.id}`);
        activate.setAttribute("aria-controls", "run-inspector");
        activate.addEventListener("click", () => selectRun(run.id));
        const dot = document.createElement("span");
        dot.className = `row-dot ${STATUS_CLASS[run.status] || ""}`;
        const label = document.createElement("span");
        label.className = "workspace-tab-label";
        label.textContent = displayName;
        const identity = document.createElement("span");
        identity.className = "workspace-tab-id";
        identity.textContent = `${run.id}`.slice(-6);
        activate.append(dot, label, identity);
        const close = document.createElement("button");
        close.type = "button";
        close.className = "workspace-tab-close";
        close.setAttribute("aria-label", `Close ${displayName} run ${run.id} view`);
        close.title = "Close view";
        close.textContent = "×";
        close.addEventListener("click", () => closeWorkspaceTab(run.id));
        tab.append(activate, close);
        tabs.append(tab);
        if (tabScrollTarget === run.id) scrollTargetElement = tab;
      }
      const addTab = document.createElement("button");
      addTab.type = "button";
      addTab.className = `workspace-add-tab${newProcessOpen ? " active" : ""}`;
      addTab.setAttribute("role", "tab");
      addTab.setAttribute("aria-label", "New Process");
      addTab.setAttribute("aria-selected", `${newProcessOpen}`);
      addTab.title = "New Process";
      addTab.textContent = "+";
      addTab.addEventListener("click", openNewProcess);
      tabs.append(addTab);
      if (tabScrollTarget === "new-process") addTab.scrollIntoView({ block: "nearest", inline: "nearest" });

      tabScrollTarget = null;
