    ## Typography
    
    ### Font Stack
    ```css
    --font-ui: 'Inter', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif;
    --font-mono: 'JetBrains Mono', 'Fira Code', 'Cascadia Code', 'Consolas', monospace;
    ```
    
    ### Scale
    | Token         | Size  | Weight | Use                        |
    |---------------|-------|--------|----------------------------|
    | `--text-xs`   | 11px  | 400    | Timestamps, badges         |
    | `--text-sm`   | 13px  | 400    | Secondary labels, captions |
    | `--text-base` | 15px  | 400    | Body text, table cells     |
    | `--text-lg`   | 18px  | 500    | Section headers            |
    | `--text-xl`   | 24px  | 600    | Panel titles               |
    | `--text-2xl`  | 32px  | 700    | Metric values              |
    | `--text-3xl`  | 40px  | 700    | Hero metrics               |
    
    ### Rules
    - UI elements: `--font-ui`
    - Data values, code, logs: `--font-mono`
    - Line height: 1.5 for body, 1.2 for headings and metrics
    - Letter spacing: -0.01em for large text, normal for body
    
    ## Spacing
    
    ### Grid
    All spacing uses a **4px base unit**:
    | Token  | Value | Use                              |
    |--------|-------|----------------------------------|
    | `--s1` | 4px   | Tight internal padding           |
    | `--s2` | 8px   | Badge padding, icon gaps         |
    | `--s3` | 12px  | List item padding                |
    | `--s4` | 16px  | Panel internal padding, card gap |
    | `--s5` | 20px  | Section spacing                  |
    | `--s6` | 24px  | Panel-to-panel gap               |
    | `--s8` | 32px  | Page margin, major sections      |
    
    ### Panel Layout
    - Panel gap: `--s4` (16px)
    - Panel padding: `--s4` (16px)
    - Panel border-radius: 8px
    - Panel border: 1px solid `--border-panel`
    - Panel background: `--bg-panel`
    
    ## Component Specifications
    
    ### Metric Card
    ```
    ┌─────────────────────────┐
    │  Label          ╱╲╱╲╱╲  │  ← sparkline (optional)
    │  1,247                   │  ← value: --text-2xl, --metric-value
    │  +12.3%                  │  ← delta: --text-sm, green/red
    └─────────────────────────┘
    ```
    - Width: min 200px, flex within grid
    - Height: auto, min ~100px
    - Background: `--bg-panel`
    - Border-radius: 8px
    - Padding: 16px
    
    ### Data Table
    ```
    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  Name ▲    Status     Value    Updated   │  ← header: --text-sm, --text-muted
    ├──────────────────────────────────────────┤
    │  Task A    ● Active   847      2m ago    │  ← row: --text-base
    │  Task B    ● Done     1.2k     5m ago    │  ← alt row: +2% white opacity
    │  Task C    ● Failed   0        12m ago   │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────┘
    ```
    - Header: uppercase, letter-spacing 0.05em, --text-muted
    - Rows: hover highlight with --hover-bg
    - Sort indicator: ▲/▼ next to active column
    - Status dots: 8px circles with semantic colors
    - Numeric values: --font-mono, right-aligned

    }
    .badge-success { background: rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.15); color: #10b981; }
    .badge-warning { background: rgba(245, 158, 11, 0.15); color: #f59e0b; }
    .badge-error   { background: rgba(239, 68, 68, 0.15);  color: #ef4444; }
    .badge-info    { background: rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.15);  color: #3b82f6; }
    ```
    
    ### Sidebar Navigation
    - Width: 220px fixed (collapsible to 56px icon-only)
    - Background: `--bg-secondary`
    - Active item: left border 3px `--border-active` + `--active-bg`
    - Items: 40px height, 16px horizontal padding
    - Icons: 20px, --text-muted (active: --text-accent)
    - Section headers: --text-xs, --text-muted, uppercase
    
    ### Live Feed / Activity Log
    - Newest at top
    - Each entry: timestamp (--text-xs, --text-muted) + icon + message
    - Timestamp format: relative ("2m ago") with hover showing absolute
    - Max visible: 50 entries, virtual scroll for more
    - Entry animation: opacity 0->1 over 200ms
    
    ## Layout Grid
    
    ### Dashboard Grid
    ```css
    .dashboard-grid {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(280px, 1fr));
      gap: var(--s4);
      padding: var(--s4);
    }
    ```
    
    ### Breakpoints
    | Name     | Width   | Columns | Notes                    |
    |----------|---------|---------|--------------------------|
    | Desktop  | 1920px+ | 4       | Full layout              |
    | Laptop   | 1366px  | 3       | Slightly compressed      |
    | Tablet   | 768px   | 2       | Stack panels             |
    | Mobile   | <768px  | 1       | Single column, no sidebar|
    
    ## Accessibility
    
    - Minimum contrast ratio: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text
    - Focus indicators: `--focus-ring` on all interactive elements
    - No information conveyed by color alone (use icons + text)
    - Keyboard navigable: Tab order follows visual order
    
    ## Animation
    
    - Transitions: 150ms ease-out for hover/active states
    - Panel entry: fade-in 200ms
    - Data updates: brief flash (100ms highlight then fade)
    - No animation on initial load (prevent layout shift)
    - Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`
    # Visual QA Checklist
    
    Run through this checklist after completing any visual change. Take a screenshot
    at each step and evaluate before proceeding.
    
    ## 1. Immediate Verification
    
    After every CSS/HTML/JS change:
    
    - [ ] Take screenshot at default viewport (1920x1080)
    - [ ] Edited component renders without layout breakage
    - [ ] No elements overflow their containers
    - [ ] Text is readable (white/light on dark backgrounds)
    - [ ] No unexpected scrollbars appeared
    
    ## 2. Color Compliance
    
    - [ ] Background colors match design system palette
    - [ ] Text colors use --text-primary, --text-secondary, or --text-muted
    - [ ] Status indicators use semantic colors (success/warning/error/info)
    - [ ] No pure white (#ffffff) backgrounds (too bright for dark theme)
    - [ ] Accent color (--text-accent / #00d4aa) used sparingly for emphasis
    - [ ] Hover/active states use the defined opacity overlays
    
    ## 3. Typography
    
    - [ ] UI text uses --font-ui (Inter/system)
    - [ ] Data values use --font-mono (JetBrains Mono)
    - [ ] Font sizes follow the type scale (no arbitrary sizes)
    - [ ] Headings use appropriate weight (500-700)
    - [ ] Body text is 15px minimum for readability
    
    ## 4. Spacing & Layout
    
    - [ ] Padding follows 4px grid (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32)
    - [ ] Panel gaps are consistent (16px)
    - [ ] Content doesn't touch panel edges (min 16px padding)
    - [ ] Vertical rhythm is consistent within panels
    - [ ] Grid layout fills available space without gaps
    
    ## 5. Components
    
    ### Metric Cards
    - [ ] Value is the most prominent element (large, bold)
    - [ ] Label is smaller and muted
    - [ ] Sparkline (if present) doesn't dominate the card
    - [ ] Card has consistent dimensions with siblings
    
    ### Tables
    - [ ] Header row is visually distinct (muted, uppercase)
    - [ ] Rows have subtle alternating backgrounds
    - [ ] Numeric columns are right-aligned
    - [ ] Status dots/badges are sized correctly (8px dots, xs text badges)
    
    ### Navigation
    - [ ] Active item clearly indicated (accent color border/background)
    - [ ] Hover states visible but not distracting
    - [ ] Icons aligned with text labels
    
    ## 6. Responsive (when layout changes are made)
    
    - [ ] Screenshot at 1920px - full layout, 4 columns
    - [ ] Screenshot at 1366px - 3 columns, nothing clipped
    - [ ] Screenshot at 768px - 2 columns or stacked
    - [ ] No horizontal scrollbar at any width above 768px
    
    ## 7. Real-Time Elements
    
    - [ ] WebSocket connection indicator visible
    - [ ] Auto-updating values don't cause layout shifts
    - [ ] Loading states shown for pending data
    - [ ] Error states displayed gracefully (not raw errors)
    
    ## 8. Final Polish
    
    - [ ] Border-radius consistent (8px panels, 4px badges)
    - [ ] Shadows subtle or absent (dark themes need minimal shadow)
    - [ ] Transitions smooth (150ms hover, 200ms panel entry)
    - [ ] No orphaned or placeholder text visible
    - [ ] Favicon loads (no browser default icon)
    
    ## Decision Framework
    
    ### Fix Without Asking
    - Color doesn't match design system palette
    - Spacing violates the 4px grid
    - Typography uses wrong font family or arbitrary size
    - Contrast ratio below 4.5:1
    - Layout breaks at standard breakpoints
    - Component doesn't match spec in design-system.md
    
    ### Escalate to User
    - Choosing between two valid layout arrangements
    - Adding or removing entire sections/panels
    - Changing the information hierarchy
    - Introducing new component types not in the design system
    - Trade-offs between data density and readability

    .workspace.explorer-collapsed .panel-foot { display: none !important; }

    .workspace-tab { width: min(220px, 25vw); min-width: 135px; display: flex; flex: none; align-items: stretch; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-bottom: 0; border-radius: 6px 6px 0 0; background: rgba(21,27,40,.62); }
    .workspace-tab.active { border-color: rgba(59,130,246,.62); background: #142338; box-shadow: inset 0 2px var(--accent); }

    function normalizeOutputLineBreaks(text, flushPendingCarriageReturn = false) {
      let normalized = "";
      if (outputPendingCarriageReturn) {
        normalized += "\n";
        if (text.startsWith("\n")) text = text.slice(1);
        outputPendingCarriageReturn = false;
      }
      for (let index = 0; index < text.length; index += 1) {
        const character = text[index];
        if (character !== "\r") {
          normalized += character;
          continue;
        }
        if (index + 1 < text.length) {
          if (text[index + 1] === "\n") index += 1;
          normalized += "\n";
        } else if (flushPendingCarriageReturn) {
          normalized += "\n";
        } else {
          outputPendingCarriageReturn = true;
        }
      }
      if (flushPendingCarriageReturn && outputPendingCarriageReturn) {
        normalized += "\n";
        outputPendingCarriageReturn = false;
      }
      return normalized;
    }

    +.run-history-section { min-width: 0; padding: 12px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 6px; background: rgba(255,255,255,.015); }
    +.history-section-heading { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: baseline; justify-content: space-between; gap: 6px; margin-bottom: 8px; }
    +.history-section-heading h3 { margin: 0; color: var(--text); font-size: 12px; }
    +.history-provenance-note { color: var(--faint); font-size: 9px; }
    +.run-events-list { display: grid; gap: 5px; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; }
    +.run-event { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 100px minmax(80px, 1fr) minmax(120px, auto); align-items: baseline; gap: 8px; padding: 6px 0; border-top: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.035); font-size: 10px; }
    +.event-provenance { color: var(--faint); font-size: 8px; text-transform: uppercase; }
    +.recorded-event .event-provenance { color: #66cdb5; }
    +.registry-event .event-provenance { color: #9aa6ba; }
    +.event-description { overflow-wrap: anywhere; color: var(--text); font-family: var(--mono); }
    +.event-timestamp { color: var(--muted); font: 9px var(--mono); text-align: right; }
    +.run-lineage-list h4 { margin: 10px 0 4px; color: var(--faint); font-size: 9px; text-transform: uppercase; }
    +.run-lineage-list ul { display: grid; gap: 7px; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; }
    +.run-lineage-list li { display: grid; min-width: 0; gap: 2px; }
    +.history-lineage-status { color: var(--faint); font-size: 9px; }
    +
    +@media (max-width: 1100px) {
    +  .history-filters { grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(110px, 1fr)); }
    +  .history-filters label:first-child { grid-column: span 2; }
    +  .run-history-details { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
    +}
    +
    +@media (max-width: 700px) {
    +  .history-view { padding: 12px; }
    +  .history-filters { grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); }
    +  .history-filters label:first-child { grid-column: span 2; }
    +  .history-table { min-width: 640px; }
    +  .run-event { grid-template-columns: minmax(75px, auto) 1fr; }
    +  .event-timestamp { grid-column: 2; text-align: left; }
    +}

    +async function testHistoricalExplorerSendsSupportedDateAndSortFilters() {
    +  const { context, requests } = dashboardHarness();
    +  const db = context.__dashboard;
    +  const opening = db.openHistoryView();
    +  await Promise.resolve();
    +  requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/api/runs/history")).resolve(response({ items: [], has_more: false }));
    +  await opening;
    +  const filtered = db.setHistoryFilter("since", "2026-10-24");
    +  await Promise.resolve();
    +  const request = requests.filter((item) => item.url.includes("/api/runs/history")).at(-1);
    +  assert.match(request.url, /since=2026-10-24T/);
    +  assert.match(request.url, /time_field=created_at/);
    +  request.resolve(response({ items: [], has_more: false }));
    +  await filtered;
    +  const sorted = db.setHistoryFilter("sort_by", "ended_at");
    +  await Promise.resolve();
    +  const sortRequest = requests.filter((item) => item.url.includes("/api/runs/history")).at(-1);
    +  assert.match(sortRequest.url, /sort_by=ended_at/);
    +  sortRequest.resolve(response({ items: [], has_more: false }));
    +  await sorted;
    +}

    "use strict";
    
    (() => {
      const PAGE_ROW_LIMIT = 200;
    
      function formatTimestamp(value) {
        if (typeof value !== "string" || !value) return "—";
        const date = new Date(value);
        return Number.isFinite(date.getTime()) ? date.toLocaleString() : "—";
      }
    
      function addCell(row, value, className = "") {
        const cell = document.createElement("td");
        if (className) cell.className = className;
        cell.textContent = value == null || value === "" ? "—" : String(value);
        row.append(cell);
        return cell;
      }
    
      function renderRunRows(body, runs, openRun) {
        body.replaceChildren();
        const boundedRuns = Array.isArray(runs) ? runs.slice(0, PAGE_ROW_LIMIT) : [];
        for (const run of boundedRuns) {
          if (!run || typeof run.id !== "string" || !run.id) continue;
          const row = document.createElement("tr");
          row.dataset.runId = run.id;
          addCell(row, typeof run.name === "string" && run.name ? run.name : "Unnamed run", "history-run-name");
    
          const status = typeof run.status === "string" && run.status ? run.status : "Unknown";
          const statusCell = addCell(row, status, `history-status status-${status.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9_-]/g, "-")}`);
          statusCell.setAttribute("aria-label", `Status: ${status}`);
    
          const idCell = document.createElement("td");
          const idButton = document.createElement("button");
          idButton.type = "button";
          idButton.className = "history-run-open";
          idButton.textContent = run.id;
          idButton.setAttribute("aria-label", `Open run ${run.id}`);
          idButton.addEventListener("click", () => openRun(run.id));
          idCell.append(idButton);
          row.append(idCell);
    
          addCell(row, formatTimestamp(run.created_at), "history-run-created");
          addCell(row, formatTimestamp(run.ended_at), "history-run-ended");
          addCell(row, run.exit_code == null ? "—" : run.exit_code, "history-run-exit-code");
          body.append(row);
        }
      }
    
      globalThis.RunmuxHistoryView = Object.freeze({ renderRunRows });
    })();

    function makeElement(tagName) {
      const listeners = new Map();
      return {
        tagName,
        children: [],
        attributes: {},
        dataset: {},
        className: "",
        _textContent: undefined,
        get textContent() {
          return this._textContent ?? this.children.map((child) => child.textContent || "").join("");
        },
        set textContent(value) { this._textContent = String(value); this.children = []; },
        append(...children) { this._textContent = undefined; this.children.push(...children); },
        replaceChildren(...children) { this._textContent = undefined; this.children = [...children]; },
        setAttribute(name, value) { this.attributes[name] = String(value); },
        addEventListener(name, callback) { listeners.set(name, callback); },
        click() { listeners.get("click")?.(); },
      };
    }
    
    const document = { createElement: makeElement };

    ---
    name: systematic-debugging
    description: Use when encountering any bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior, before proposing fixes
    ---
    
    # Systematic Debugging
    
    ## Overview
    
    **Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.
    
    **Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**
    
    ## The Iron Law
    
    ```
    NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
    ```
    
    If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.
    
    ## When to Use
    
    Use for ANY technical issue:
    - Test failures
    - Bugs in production
    - Unexpected behavior
    - Performance problems
    - Build failures
    - Integration issues
    
    **Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
    - Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
    - "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
    - You've already tried multiple fixes
    - Previous fix didn't work
    - You don't fully understand the issue
    
    **Don't skip when:**
    - Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
    - You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
    - Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)
    
    ## The Four Phases
    
    You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
    
    ### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation
    
    **BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**
    
    1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
       - Don't skip past errors or warnings
       - They often contain the exact solution
       - Read stack traces completely
       - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes
    
    2. **Reproduce Consistently**
       - Can you trigger it reliably?
       - What are the exact steps?
       - Does it happen every time?
       - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess
    
    3. **Check Recent Changes**
       - What changed that could cause this?
       - Git diff, recent commits
       - New dependencies, config changes
       - Environmental differences
    
    4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**
    
       **WHEN system has multiple components (CI → build → signing, API → service → database):**
    
       **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
       ```
       For EACH component boundary:
         - Log what data enters component
         - Log what data exits component
         - Verify environment/config propagation
         - Check state at each layer
    
       Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
       THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
       THEN investigate that specific component
       ```
    
       **Example (multi-layer system):**
       ```bash
       # Layer 1: Workflow
       echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
       echo "IDENTITY: $([ -n "${IDENTITY:-}" ] && echo SET || echo UNSET)"
    
       # Layer 2: Build script
       echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
       printenv IDENTITY >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "IDENTITY in environment" || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"
    
       # Layer 3: Signing script
       echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
       security list-keychains
       security find-identity -v
    
       # Layer 4: Actual signing
       codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
       ```
    
       **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets → workflow ✓, workflow → build ✗)
    
    5. **Trace Data Flow**
    
       **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**
    
       See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.
    
       **Quick version:**
       - Where does bad value originate?
       - What called this with bad value?
       - Keep tracing up until you find the source
       - Fix at source, not at symptom
    
    ### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis
    
    **Find the pattern before fixing:**
    
    1. **Find Working Examples**
       - Locate similar working code in same codebase
       - What works that's similar to what's broken?
    
    2. **Compare Against References**
       - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
       - Don't skim - read every line
       - Understand the pattern fully before applying
    
    3. **Identify Differences**
       - What's different between working and broken?
       - List every difference, however small
       - Don't assume "that can't matter"
    
    4. **Understand Dependencies**
       - What other components does this need?
       - What settings, config, environment?
       - What assumptions does it make?
    
    ### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing
    
    **Scientific method:**
    
    1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
       - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
       - Write it down
       - Be specific, not vague
    
    2. **Test Minimally**
       - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
       - One variable at a time
       - Don't fix multiple things at once
    
    3. **Verify Before Continuing**
       - Did it work? Yes → Phase 4
       - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
       - DON'T add more fixes on top
    
    4. **When You Don't Know**
       - Say "I don't understand X"
       - Don't pretend to know
       - Ask for help
       - Research more
    
    ### Phase 4: Implementation
    
    **Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**
    
    1. **Create Failing Test Case**
       - Simplest possible reproduction
       - Automated test if possible
       - One-off test script if no framework
       - MUST have before fixing
       - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests
    
    2. **Implement Single Fix**
       - Address the root cause identified
       - ONE change at a time
       - No "while I'm here" improvements
       - No bundled refactoring
    
    3. **Verify Fix**
       - Test passes now?
       - No other tests broken?
       - Issue actually resolved?
       - Use the `superpowers:verification-before-completion` skill before claiming success
    
    4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**
       - STOP
       - Count: How many fixes have you tried?
       - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information
       - **If ≥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**
       - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion
    
    5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**
    
       **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**
       - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place
       - Fixes require "massive refactoring" to implement
       - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere
    
       **STOP and question fundamentals:**
       - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?
       - Are we "sticking with it through sheer inertia"?
       - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?
    
       **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**
    
       This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.
    
    ## Red Flags - STOP and Follow Process
    
    If you catch yourself thinking:
    - "Quick fix for now, investigate later"
    - "Just try changing X and see if it works"
    - "Add multiple changes, run tests"
    - "Skip the test, I'll manually verify"
    - "It's probably X, let me fix that"
    - "I don't fully understand but this might work"
    - "Pattern says X but I'll adapt it differently"
    - "Here are the main problems: [lists fixes without investigation]"
    - Proposing solutions before tracing data flow
    - **"One more fix attempt" (when already tried 2+)**
    - **Each fix reveals new problem in different place**
    
    **ALL of these mean: STOP. Return to Phase 1.**
    
    **If 3+ fixes failed:** Question the architecture (see Phase 4.5)
    
    ## your human partner's Signals You're Doing It Wrong
    
    **Watch for these redirections:**
    - "Is that not happening?" - You assumed without verifying
    - "Will it show us...?" - You should have added evidence gathering
    - "Stop guessing" - You're proposing fixes without understanding
    - "Ultra-think this" - Question fundamentals, not just symptoms
    - "We're stuck?" (frustrated) - Your approach isn't working
    
    **When you see these:** STOP. Return to Phase 1.
    
    ## Common Rationalizations
    
    | Excuse | Reality |
    |--------|---------|
    | "Issue is simple, don't need process" | Simple issues have root causes too. Process is fast for simple bugs. |
    | "Emergency, no time for process" | Systematic debugging is FASTER than guess-and-check thrashing. |
    | "Just try this first, then investigate" | First fix sets the pattern. Do it right from the start. |
    | "I'll write test after confirming fix works" | Untested fixes don't stick. Test first proves it. |
    | "Multiple fixes at once saves time" | Can't isolate what worked. Causes new bugs. |
    | "Reference too long, I'll adapt the pattern" | Partial understanding guarantees bugs. Read it completely. |
    | "I see the problem, let me fix it" | Seeing symptoms ≠ understanding root cause. |
    | "One more fix attempt" (after 2+ failures) | 3+ failures = architectural problem. Question pattern, don't fix again. |
    
    ## Quick Reference
    
    | Phase | Key Activities | Success Criteria |
    |-------|---------------|------------------|
    | **1. Root Cause** | Read errors, reproduce, check changes, gather evidence | Understand WHAT and WHY |
    | **2. Pattern** | Find working examples, compare | Identify differences |
    | **3. Hypothesis** | Form theory, test minimally | Confirmed or new hypothesis |
    | **4. Implementation** | Create test, fix, verify | Bug resolved, tests pass |
    
    ## When Process Reveals "No Root Cause"
    
    If systematic investigation reveals issue is truly environmental, timing-dependent, or external:
    
    1. You've completed the process
    2. Document what you investigated
    3. Implement appropriate handling (retry, timeout, error message)
    4. Add monitoring/logging for future investigation
    
    **But:** 95% of "no root cause" cases are incomplete investigation.
    
    ## Supporting Techniques
    
    These techniques are part of systematic debugging and available in this directory:
    
    - **`root-cause-tracing.md`** - Trace bugs backward through call stack to find original trigger
    - **`defense-in-depth.md`** - Add validation at multiple layers after finding root cause
    - **`condition-based-waiting.md`** - Replace arbitrary timeouts with condition polling

Yes. **Two was only the number of `opencode_fire` coding-task dispatches.** It was wrong to present that as the number of OpenCode calls.

Here’s the fuller inventory I can verify:

- **Gate A `opencode_setup`** — checked the connected OpenCode runtime. It returned that OpenCode and the LM Studio provider were ready; this did not ask the model to code.
- **Gate A `opencode_context`** — checked the selected model/roles. It returned `lmstudio/qwen38_23GB` and the available worker roles; also not a coding request.
- **Gate B `opencode_setup`** — verified the `lmstudio` provider and `local-worker` role before the required smoke test.
- **Gate B `opencode_fire`** — actual local task: fix the one-line retry backoff defect in the disposable fixture, edit only `src/retry_policy.py`, run pytest, preserve the sentinel. The worker made that edit and reported 3 passing tests; I independently verified the diff, tests, and sentinel.
- **Gate B observation calls** — I used OpenCode status/conversation tools to inspect completion and evidence. The compacted history I have does not retain their exact number/order, so I can’t honestly itemize those individual polls.
- **Phase 6C `opencode_fire`** — actual local task: build the bounded historical table renderer and focused tests, limited to `history_view.js` and `history_view_test.js`. It returned no changes. After about 14 minutes and extensive harness exploration, I cancelled it.
- **Phase 6C observation calls** — I can verify these individual calls: `opencode_check`, `opencode_conversation(limit: 4)`, `opencode_check(detailed)`, `opencode_conversation(limit: 6)`, `opencode_wait(45s)`, `opencode_check`, `opencode_conversation(limit: 2)`, `opencode_wait(60s)`, `opencode_check`, and `opencode_job_cancel`. They returned progress/tool traces and ultimately cancellation with zero changed files; none dispatched a new task.

So there were **two coding-task dispatches**, plus multiple setup, context, observation, and cancellation calls. I should have made that distinction from the start.

    .history-open-button { padding: 5px 8px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 5px; color: var(--text); }
    .history-open-button:hover { border-color: rgba(0,212,170,.4); }
    .history-workspace-tab { width: auto; padding-inline: 10px; color: var(--text); font-size: 11px; }
    .history-view { display: flex; min-width: 0; min-height: 0; flex: 1; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; overflow: auto; padding: 20px; }
    .history-view-header { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px; padding-bottom: 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); }
    .history-view-header h2 { margin: 3px 0 4px; font-size: 18px; }
    .history-view-header p { margin: 0; color: var(--muted); font-size: 11px; }
    .history-presets { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 6px; }
    .history-preset { padding: 6px 10px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 5px; background: rgba(255,255,255,.02); color: var(--muted); font-size: 10px; }
    .history-preset:hover, .history-preset.active { border-color: rgba(0,212,170,.35); background: rgba(0,212,170,.08); color: var(--text); }
    .history-filters { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(150px, 2fr) repeat(3, minmax(105px, 1fr)) repeat(2, minmax(130px, 1fr)) minmax(70px, .55fr) auto auto; align-items: end; gap: 8px; }
    .history-filters label { display: grid; min-width: 0; gap: 4px; color: var(--muted); font-size: 9px; letter-spacing: .04em; text-transform: uppercase; }
    .history-filters input, .history-filters select { width: 100%; min-width: 0; height: 32px; padding: 0 8px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 4px; outline: none; background: var(--input); color: var(--text); font: 10px var(--mono); text-transform: none; }
    .history-filters input:focus, .history-filters select:focus { border-color: rgba(0,212,170,.55); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(0,212,170,.12); }
    .history-apply-button { min-height: 32px; padding: 0 10px; font-size: 10px; }
    .history-filters .quiet-button { height: 32px; padding-inline: 10px; border: 1px solid var(--border); }
    .history-state, .history-detail-state { min-height: 20px; color: var(--muted); font-size: 10px; }
    .history-table-scroll { min-height: 0; overflow: auto; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 6px; }
    .history-table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; table-layout: fixed; }
    .history-table th { position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 1; padding: 9px 10px; background: #141b25; color: var(--faint); font-size: 9px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: .06em; text-align: left; text-transform: uppercase; }
    .history-table td { overflow: hidden; padding: 8px 10px; border-top: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.035); color: var(--text); font-size: 10px; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }
    .history-table tbody tr:nth-child(even) { background: rgba(255,255,255,.018); }
    .history-table tbody tr:hover { background: rgba(0,212,170,.055); }
    .history-table th:nth-child(1) { width: 20%; }
    .history-table th:nth-child(2) { width: 12%; }
    .history-table th:nth-child(3) { width: 25%; }
    .history-table th:nth-child(4), .history-table th:nth-child(5) { width: 19%; }
    .history-table th:nth-child(6) { width: 5%; text-align: right; }
    .history-table td:last-child { font-family: var(--mono); text-align: right; }
    .history-run-id-button, .history-lineage-link, .history-relation-link { max-width: 100%; overflow: hidden; padding: 0; border: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--accent); font: 10px var(--mono); text-align: left; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }
    .history-run-id-button:hover, .history-lineage-link:hover, .history-relation-link:hover { text-decoration: underline; }
    .history-status { display: inline-flex; padding: 2px 6px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.08); border-radius: 4px; color: var(--muted); font-size: 8px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .05em; text-transform: uppercase; }
    .history-status.failed, .history-status.lost, .history-status.killed { border-color: rgba(239,68,68,.2); background: rgba(239,68,68,.1); color: #ff8585; }
    .history-status.finished { border-color: rgba(16,185,129,.2); background: rgba(16,185,129,.08); color: #54d1a1; }
    .history-status.running, .history-status.pending, .history-status.paused { border-color: rgba(245,158,11,.2); background: rgba(245,158,11,.08); color: #f7bd52; }
    .history-pagination { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 14px; min-height: 32px; color: var(--muted); font: 10px var(--mono); }
    .history-pagination button:disabled { opacity: .4; cursor: default; }
    .run-history-details { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1.15fr) minmax(0, .85fr); gap: 12px; margin-top: 18px; }
    .run-history-section { min-width: 0; padding: 12px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 6px; background: rgba(255,255,255,.015); }
    .history-section-heading { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: baseline; justify-content: space-between; gap: 6px; margin-bottom: 8px; }
    .history-section-heading h3 { margin: 0; color: var(--text); font-size: 12px; }
    .history-provenance-note { color: var(--faint); font-size: 9px; }
    .run-events-list { display: grid; gap: 5px; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; }
    .run-event { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 100px minmax(80px, 1fr) minmax(120px, auto); align-items: baseline; gap: 8px; padding: 6px 0; border-top: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.035); font-size: 10px; }
    .event-provenance { color: var(--faint); font-size: 8px; text-transform: uppercase; }
    .recorded-event .event-provenance { color: #66cdb5; }
    .registry-event .event-provenance { color: #9aa6ba; }
    .event-description { overflow-wrap: anywhere; color: var(--text); font-family: var(--mono); }
    .event-timestamp { color: var(--muted); font: 9px var(--mono); text-align: right; }
    .run-lineage-list h4 { margin: 10px 0 4px; color: var(--faint); font-size: 9px; text-transform: uppercase; }
    .run-lineage-list ul { display: grid; gap: 7px; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; }
    .run-lineage-list li { display: grid; min-width: 0; gap: 2px; }
    .history-lineage-status { color: var(--faint); font-size: 9px; }
    
    @media (max-width: 1100px) {
      .history-filters { grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(110px, 1fr)); }
      .history-filters label:first-child { grid-column: span 2; }
      .run-history-details { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
    }
    
    @media (max-width: 700px) {
      .history-view { padding: 12px; }

    # Runmux Current Handoff
    
    ## Runmux Web UI — Phase 4A integrated (Backend and Frontend)
    
    Phase 4A (Lifecycle Controls Backend and Frontend) is fully integrated and merged into `main` from `codex/runmux-lifecycle-backend-20261024` and `codex/runmux-web-lifecycle-frontend-20261024` with no conflicts.
    It provides authenticated, same-origin REST lifecycle endpoints (`POST /api/runs/{run_id}/stop`, `POST /api/runs/{run_id}/kill`, `POST /api/runs/{run_id}/restart`, `POST /api/runs/{run_id}/duplicate`, `POST /api/runs/{run_id}/pause`, `POST /api/runs/{run_id}/resume`, `GET /api/capabilities`) with state machine validation, supervisor PID reuse protection, and inconclusive process identity fallback safety.
    In the browser, it provides selected-process controls for graceful Stop (`force: false`), forced Kill (`force: true`), Restart (creating a new immutable Run ID, reconciling tabs), Duplicate, and capability-aware Pause/Resume (disabled on Windows with descriptive tooltip; dynamic Resume action for paused processes). Destructive actions require modal confirmation displaying the process name and full immutable 22-character Run ID.
    Verified with Python test suites (`lifecycle_test.py`, `lifecycle_api_test.py`, `web_test.py`), Node unit suite (`dashboard_test.js`), and headless Chrome CDP E2E testing (`browser_e2e_test.js`).
    See `plans/20261024-1315_runmux-web-lifecycle-frontend/HANDOFF.md`, `STATUS.md`, and `plans/20261024-runmux-lifecycle-backend/HANDOFF.md`.
    
    ## Runmux Web UI — Phase 5A+ integrated
    
    Phase 5A+ (Overview Modes & Live Telemetry Frontend) was merged into `main` from `codex/runmux-web-overview-telemetry-20261024` with no conflicts.
    It provides four selectable overview densities (Mode A Minimal, Mode B Inline, Mode C Dashboard, Mode D Expanded) with keyboard/button cycling and browser persistence, consumes Phase 5B live telemetry endpoints, correctly handles stale ISO 8601 timestamps, separates hardware vs per-process GPU attribution, and respects request cancellation and background throttling.
    Verified with headless Chrome CDP, Node unit tests, and Python test suites.
    See `plans/20261024-runmux-web-overview-telemetry/HANDOFF.md` and `STATUS.md`.
    
    ## Runmux Web UI — Phase 4B integrated
    
    Phase 4B (Enhanced Output Search and Filtering) was merged into `main` from `codex/runmux-web-phase4b-20261024` with no conflicts.
    It provides bounded Output search, highlighted matches, safe literal search with ReDoS protection, DOM element bounding (`MAX_RENDER_LINES = 2000`, `MAX_RENDER_MATCHES = 500`), next/previous navigation, conservative severity filtering (`all`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `other`), and accurate count/scope labeling.
    Verified with headless Chrome CDP, Node unit tests, and Python test suites.
    See `plans/20261024-runmux-web-enhanced-logs/HANDOFF.md` and `STATUS.md`.

    # Runmux Phase 6C Historical Explorer Frontend
    
    **Date:** 2026-10-24
    **Branch:** `codex/runmux-6c-history-frontend-local-pilot-20261024`
    **Worktree:** `.worktrees/runmux-6c-history-frontend-local-pilot`
    **Baseline:** `4591b3247bdfafe82f0b8d1a73f40002152a6c2b`
    **Scope:** Browser implementation of Phase 6C historical run discovery, lifecycle event presentation, and explicit restart/duplicate lineage.
    
    ## Goal and boundaries
    
    Add a bounded, paginated History workspace view using the existing authenticated Phase 6C endpoints. Preserve the current process explorer, process tabs, Output, Terminal, Details, lifecycle controls, and Phase 5C charts. Keep Run ID as the only run identity. Do not change API contracts, backend behavior, telemetry retention, event persistence, supervisor behavior, or other Phase 6 slices.
    
    The browser must not disclose arguments, working directories, environment data, or credentials. Closing the History view or a process tab remains view-only. Persisted telemetry events and registry-derived timestamp markers must be visibly labeled by provenance; missing events or relationships remain explicitly empty/unavailable.
    
    ## Approaches considered
    
    1. **Add filters to the live process explorer.** This would reuse its location, but risks replacing or overloading the active-run workflow and cannot cleanly represent cursor pages plus historical event/lineage detail.
    2. **Open a modal history browser.** This would avoid changing workspace tabs, but gives a large table, filter controls, pagination, and event detail too little space and creates nested navigation.
    3. **Add a dedicated History workspace tab (selected).** It preserves the process explorer and existing run tabs, provides adequate room for filters and a bounded table, and can open any row into the existing immutable Run ID view. The existing Details area will host per-run events and explicit lineage navigation.
    
    ## Data and interaction contract
    
    - Query only `GET /api/runs/history`; default to 50 items and keep every response bounded. Use cursor history for Previous/Next navigation; never load the entire registry. Do not request exact totals by default.
    - Use only API-supported filters and sort keys: status/state, name, inclusive `since`/`until` with `time_field`, exit code, failed/lost, restart/duplicate parent, and restart existence; sort by `created_at`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `name`, or `numeric_id` with supported direction.
    - Reset cursors on filter/sort changes. Abort or disregard stale requests when filters, page, selected Run ID, or workspace change. Render at most one server page (maximum 200) plus bounded event/lineage views.
    - Opening a row selects/opens the existing run view using its full immutable Run ID. Duplicate names never share state. The History workspace tab and per-run tabs are view-only.
    - Fetch `/api/runs/{run_id}/events` and `/lineage` only for the selected run's Details view. Label `telemetry_store` as recorded telemetry and `registry_record` as a registry timestamp/relationship marker. No inferred lifecycle events. Navigate only by explicit relationship Run IDs.
    - Use text nodes/textContent for server values. The backend allowlist is the source for safe fields; never render private command arguments, cwd, environment, or secrets.
    - Preserve the established dark IDE styling and responsive behavior. Do not modify Phase 5C chart semantics or address issue #11.
    
    ## Stages and acceptance
    
    1. **Contract and plan:** verify endpoint parameters, cursor/filter binding, authentication inheritance, event provenance, lineage IDs, privacy allowlist, and Phase 5C integration. (Complete.)
    2. **Presentational helper:** add a bounded table/event/lineage rendering helper and deterministic unit coverage in files owned solely by the local worker; coordinator reviews before integration.
    3. **Controller and markup:** add the History workspace view, supported filter/sort controls, cursor stack, request cancellation/generation guards, and safe navigation while retaining existing tabs and controls.
    4. **Details integration:** render event provenance and explicit lineage in selected-run Details with missing-run, no-event, and API error states.
    5. **Validation:** run JS unit tests, focused Python API/adapter tests with explicit worktree `PYTHONPATH`, and real headless Chrome E2E against only synthetic registry/telemetry state and a dedicated loopback port. Check desktop/responsive screenshots, duplicate names, request bounds, stale responses, expired auth, malformed filters, missing runs, and unchanged process-control behavior.
    6. **Review and publication:** inspect the complete diff, record screenshots, exact validation and limitations, commit the feature branch, push it, and leave it unmerged for independent GPT-6.1 Sol Medium audit.
    
    ## Baseline evidence
    
    - Branch/worktree at the pinned commit was clean before implementation.
    - `node modules/runmux/tests/dashboard_test.js` passed on the baseline.
    - `node modules/runmux/tests/browser_e2e_test.js` initially could not start its disposable loopback server inside the socket sandbox. The same command passed after an approved elevated run, using disposable state and real headless Chrome. This is an environment boundary, not an application defect.
    - Backend history/API tests and handoff confirm a 1–200 run page cap, 1–1,000 event cap, supported sort/filter set, cursor-bound filters/sort, authenticated `/api`, safe metadata allowlists, explicit event provenance, and explicit restart/duplicate Run IDs. The backend does not provide a cross-request snapshot; status changes may affect later page membership.

    def test_ten_thousand_run_registry_queries_remain_page_bounded(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        store = RunStore(tmp_path)
        base = "2026-10-24T12:00:00+00:00"
        with sqlite3.connect(store.db_path) as connection:
            connection.executemany(
                """INSERT INTO runs (
                    id, numeric_id, name, status, created_at, updated_at, started_at, ended_at, exit_code,
                    program, argv_json, cwd, env_overrides_json, auth_token, log_path, command_line,
                    restart_of, duplicate_of, rows, columns
                ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, NULL, ?, ?, ?, '[]', '/', '{}', 'token', '/secret/path', 'cmd',
                    NULL, NULL, 24, 80)""",
                (
                    (
                        f"20261024-120000-{index:06x}",
                        index,
                        f"worker-{index % 100}",
                        "failed" if index % 10 == 0 else "finished",
                        f"2026-10-24T12:{index // 600:02d}:{(index // 10) % 60:02d}+00:00",
                        base,
                        base,
                        1 if index % 10 == 0 else 0,
                        sys.executable,
                    )
                    for index in range(10_000)
                ),
            )
    
        start = time.perf_counter()
        first = store.query_runs(limit=50)
        first_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
        start = time.perf_counter()
        middle = store.query_runs(limit=50, cursor=first.next_cursor)
        next_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
        start = time.perf_counter()
        filtered = store.query_runs(limit=50, status="failed", name="worker-2")
        filtered_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
    
        assert len(first.items) == len(middle.items) == len(filtered.items) == 50
        assert all(record.status == "failed" and "worker-2" in (record.name or "") for record in filtered.items)
        print(f"10k registry query benchmark: first={first_ms:.2f}ms next={next_ms:.2f}ms filtered={filtered_ms:.2f}ms")
      assert.match(feedbackBanner.textContent, /not supported on Windows/i);
    }
    
    async function testHistoricalExplorerUsesBoundedCursorPages() {
      const { context, requests } = dashboardHarness();
      const db = context.__dashboard;
      const opening = db.openHistoryView();
      await Promise.resolve();
      const firstPage = requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/api/runs/history"));
      assert.ok(firstPage, `History view must use the dedicated history API; requests: ${requests.map((request) => request.url).join(", ")}`);
      assert.match(firstPage.url, /limit=50/);
      assert.match(firstPage.url, /sort_by=created_at/);
      assert.doesNotMatch(firstPage.url, /include_total=true/);
      assert.doesNotMatch(firstPage.url, /\/api\/runs(?:\?|$)/, "History must not retrieve the full registry");
      firstPage.resolve(response({
        items: [{ id: "run-a", name: "duplicate name", status: "finished", created_at: "2026-10-24T10:00:00Z" }],
        next_cursor: "opaque-next", has_more: true, page_size: 1, total_count: null,
      }));
      await opening;
      assert.equal(db.historyState().items[0].id, "run-a");
      assert.equal(db.historyState().hasMore, true);
    
      const next = db.goHistoryPage("next");
      await Promise.resolve();
      const nextPage = requests.filter((request) => request.url.includes("/api/runs/history")).at(-1);
      assert.match(nextPage.url, /cursor=opaque-next/);
      nextPage.resolve(response({ items: [], next_cursor: null, has_more: false, page_size: 0, total_count: null }));
      await next;
      assert.equal(db.historyState().pageIndex, 1);
      assert.equal(db.historyState().items.length, 0);
      const beforeClose = requests.length;
      db.closeHistoryView();
      assert.equal(requests.length, beforeClose, "Closing the history view must not dispatch any process lifecycle request");
    }
    
    async function testHistoricalExplorerSendsSupportedDateAndSortFilters() {
      const { context, requests } = dashboardHarness();
      const db = context.__dashboard;
      const opening = db.openHistoryView();
      await Promise.resolve();
      requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/api/runs/history")).resolve(response({ items: [], has_more: false }));
      await opening;
      const filtered = db.setHistoryFilter("since", "2026-10-24");
      await Promise.resolve();
      const request = requests.filter((item) => item.url.includes("/api/runs/history")).at(-1);
      assert.match(request.url, /since=2026-10-24T/);
      assert.match(request.url, /time_field=created_at/);
      request.resolve(response({ items: [], has_more: false }));
      await filtered;
      const sorted = db.setHistoryFilter("sort_by", "ended_at");
      await Promise.resolve();
      const sortRequest = requests.filter((item) => item.url.includes("/api/runs/history")).at(-1);
      assert.match(sortRequest.url, /sort_by=ended_at/);
      sortRequest.resolve(response({ items: [], has_more: false }));
      await sorted;
    }
    
    async function testHistoricalExplorerIgnoresObsoleteFilterResponses() {
      const { context, requests } = dashboardHarness();
      const db = context.__dashboard;
      const initial = db.openHistoryView();
      await Promise.resolve();
      const first = requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/api/runs/history"));
      const filtered = db.setHistoryFilter("name", "new query");
      await Promise.resolve();
      const second = requests.filter((request) => request.url.includes("/api/runs/history")).at(-1);
      assert.notEqual(first, second);
      assert.equal(first.options.signal.aborted, true, "Changing filters should abort an obsolete history request");
      assert.match(second.url, /name=new\+query|name=new%20query/);
      second.resolve(response({ items: [{ id: "fresh-id", name: "fresh", status: "lost" }], next_cursor: null, has_more: false, page_size: 1 }));
      await filtered;
      first.resolve(response({ items: [{ id: "stale-id", name: "stale", status: "finished" }], next_cursor: null, has_more: false, page_size: 1 }));
      await initial;
      assert.equal(db.historyState().items[0].id, "fresh-id");
    }
    
    async function testHistoricalExplorerReportsApiErrorsAndUnauthorizedSessions() {
      const failed = dashboardHarness();
      const failedDb = failed.context.__dashboard;
      const failureLoad = failedDb.openHistoryView();
      await Promise.resolve();
      failed.requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/api/runs/history")).resolve(response({ detail: "bad sort key" }, 400));
      await failureLoad;
      assert.match(failed.getElement("#history-state").textContent, /filters were rejected/i);
    
      const unauthorized = dashboardHarness();
      const unauthorizedLoad = unauthorized.context.__dashboard.openHistoryView();
      await Promise.resolve();
      unauthorized.requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/api/runs/history")).resolve(response({ detail: "expired" }, 401));
      await unauthorizedLoad;
      assert.equal(unauthorized.getElement("#dashboard").hidden, true);
      assert.match(unauthorized.getElement("#login-error").textContent, /session expired/i);
    }
    
    async function testRunDetailsShowEventProvenanceAndExplicitLineage() {
      const { context, requests, getElement } = dashboardHarness();
      const db = context.__dashboard;
      db.setSelectedId("run-current");
      const details = db.refreshRunHistoryDetails("run-current");
      await Promise.resolve();
      const eventsRequest = requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/events?"));
      const lineageRequest = requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/lineage?"));
      assert.match(eventsRequest.url, /limit=100/);
      assert.match(lineageRequest.url, /limit=200/);
      eventsRequest.resolve(response({ run_id: "run-current", has_more: false, events: [
        { event_type: "pause", timestamp: "2026-10-24T10:00:00Z", provenance: "telemetry_store", reason: "private reason" },
        { event_type: "registered", timestamp: "2026-10-24T09:00:00Z", provenance: "registry_record", related_run_id: "run-parent" },
      ] }));
      lineageRequest.resolve(response({ run_id: "run-current", root_run_id: "run-parent", ancestors: [
        { id: "run-parent", name: "same name", status: "finished", created_at: "2026-10-24T08:00:00Z", relationship: "parent_restart" },
      ], descendants: [{ id: "run-child", name: "same name", status: "failed", created_at: "2026-10-24T11:00:00Z", relationship: "child_duplicate" }], truncated: false }));
      await details;
      const eventsText = getElement("#run-events-list").textContent;
      assert.match(eventsText, /Recorded event/);
      assert.match(eventsText, /Registry timestamp/);
      assert.doesNotMatch(eventsText, /private reason/);
      assert.match(getElement("#run-lineage-list").textContent, /Restarted from: same name · run-parent/);
      assert.match(getElement("#run-lineage-list").textContent, /Duplicated by: same name · run-child/);
    }
    
    async function testRunDetailsRepresentMissingEventsAndLineageHonestly() {
      const { context, requests, getElement } = dashboardHarness();
      const db = context.__dashboard;
      db.setSelectedId("orphan-run");
      const details = db.refreshRunHistoryDetails("orphan-run");
      await Promise.resolve();
      requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/events?")).resolve(response({ events: [], has_more: false }));
      requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/lineage?")).resolve(response({ ancestors: [], descendants: [], truncated: false }));
      await details;
      assert.match(getElement("#run-events-state").textContent, /no lifecycle events or registry timestamp markers/i);
      assert.match(getElement("#run-lineage-state").textContent, /no recorded restart or duplicate relationships/i);
    }
    
    async function testRunDetailsReportMissingRunsAndApiFailures() {
      const { context, requests, getElement } = dashboardHarness();
      const db = context.__dashboard;
      db.setSelectedId("removed-run");
      const details = db.refreshRunHistoryDetails("removed-run");
      await Promise.resolve();
      requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/events?")).resolve(response({ detail: "Run not found" }, 404));
      requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/lineage?")).resolve(response({ detail: "registry unavailable" }, 503));
      await details;
      assert.match(getElement("#run-events-state").textContent, /no longer present in the registry/i);
      assert.match(getElement("#run-lineage-state").textContent, /temporarily unavailable/i);
    }

## Addendum — Adaptive Delegation for Newly Discovered Tasks

The D0–D7 allocation establishes the initial execution plan, **not an exhaustive or immutable division of responsibilities**.

During implementation, if additional tasks or subtasks are discovered, the Codex coordinator is responsible for deciding whether to execute them directly or delegate them to the local model.

### 1. Dynamic routing decisions

For every newly discovered substantive task, evaluate:

- **Clarity:** Are the requirements and expected results sufficiently defined?
- **Complexity:** Can the work be bounded into a manageable, coherent assignment?
- **Dependencies:** Can required contracts, fixtures, and context be supplied without extensive independent discovery?
- **Verification:** Can the result be independently checked with tests, diffs, or deterministic acceptance criteria?
- **Risk:** Could an incorrect implementation compromise security, process state, data integrity, or API compatibility?
- **Efficiency:** Is local delegation likely to reduce coordinator effort after accounting for preparation, execution, verification, and potential rework?

**Prefer local-worker implementation when requirements are clear, changes are bounded, risks are manageable, and verification is straightforward.**

Retain tasks with Codex when they involve unresolved architectural decisions, high-risk integration, security-sensitive behavior, or substantial cross-component reasoning.

Do not automatically retain tasks merely because they touch existing files or were not listed in D0–D7.

### 2. Adaptive task decomposition

When a task is too broad for efficient local execution, consider splitting it into:

1. Coordinator-owned contract clarification and architecture.
2. Local-worker implementation of bounded components.
3. Coordinator-owned integration and independent verification.

Do not split tasks into trivial fragments solely to increase delegation counts.

Use sequential ownership when multiple tasks modify the same files.

### 3. Learning from previous outcomes

Adjust routing decisions based on actual worker performance.

If Qwen repeatedly struggles with a task category, consider improving its supplied context, narrowing the task, or retaining similar work with Codex.

If Qwen successfully handles a task category with minimal rework, consider delegating more work of that type.

The objective is to optimize **net useful work, quality, completion time, and cloud-model resource consumption**, not to maximize delegation frequency.

### 4. Record decisions

For every newly discovered substantive task, add an entry to `LOCAL_DISPATCH_LEDGER.md` describing:

- Task and category.
- Chosen executor: Codex or local-worker.
- Reason for the routing decision.
- Expected verification method.
- Actual outcome, including rework and time where measurable.
- Whether the routing decision would be repeated.

Record tasks retained by Codex as well as delegated tasks. No need to log trivial individual tool calls as separate tasks.

### 5. Authority and scope

The coordinator may autonomously route, decompose, and implement newly discovered tasks **within the already approved Phase 6C frontend scope**.

Do not interpret this flexibility as authorization for unrelated features, backend redesigns, additional phases, or changes to global agent configurations.

Follow existing file ownership, safety, validation, and publication constraints.

Routine routing decisions do not require user approval. Escalate only material product decisions, security-policy questions, scope expansions, or actions outside existing authorization.

**The coordinator remains accountable for the correctness of all results, regardless of which model performs the implementation.**

    def test_query_runs_filters_are_applied_in_sql_and_run_ids_remain_identity(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        store = RunStore(tmp_path)
        created = "2026-10-24T12:00:00+00:00"
        _insert_run(
            store, "20261024-120000-000001", created_at=created, ended_at=created, name="Same", status="failed", exit_code=2
        )
        _insert_run(
            store,
            "20261024-120000-000002",
            created_at=created,
            ended_at=created,
            name="Same",
            status="finished",
            exit_code=0,
        )
        _insert_run(
            store,
            "20261024-120000-000003",
            created_at=created,
            ended_at=created,
            name="Other",
            status="lost",
            exit_code=None,
        )
    
        page = store.query_runs(name="same", failed_only=True)
        assert [record.id for record in page.items] == ["20261024-120000-000001"]
        assert [record.id for record in store.query_runs(lost_only=True).items] == ["20261024-120000-000003"]
        assert store.query_runs(state="terminal", limit=1).page_size == 1
        bounded = store.query_runs(
            since="2026-10-24T12:00:00Z",
            until=1792843200,
            time_field="ended_at",
            name="same",
            sort_by="numeric_id",
            sort_dir="asc",
            include_total=True,
        )
        assert [record.id for record in bounded.items] == ["20261024-120000-000001", "20261024-120000-000002"]
        assert bounded.total_count == 2
    
    
    def test_lineage_uses_explicit_restart_and_duplicate_ids(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        store = RunStore(tmp_path)
        created = "2026-10-24T12:00:00+00:00"
        root = "20261024-120000-000001"
        restarted = "20261024-120001-000002"
        duplicate = "20261024-120002-000003"
        _insert_run(store, root, created_at=created)
        _insert_run(store, restarted, created_at=created, restart_of=root)
        _insert_run(store, duplicate, created_at=created, duplicate_of=root)
    
        lineage = store.get_run_lineage(root)
        assert lineage.root_run_id == root
        assert lineage.ancestors == []
        assert {node.id for node in lineage.descendants} == {restarted, duplicate}
        assert lineage.total_restarts == 1
        assert lineage.total_duplicates == 1
        restarted_lineage = store.get_run_lineage(restarted)
        assert [(node.id, node.relationship) for node in restarted_lineage.ancestors] == [(root, "parent_restart")]

      if (preset === "completed") runHistoryFilters.status = "finished";
      if (preset === "failed") runHistoryFilters.failed_only = true;

      $("#history-sort-dir").value = runHistoryFilters.sort_dir;

    This is coordinator-prepared input for D1–D3. The backend/API contract is established; do not change it.
    
    ## Current source and test locations

    - Existing live-browser tests: `modules/runmux/tests/browser_e2e_test.js`, Phase 6C section beginning around line 530; viewport loop around line 850.
    - API contract: `modules/runmux/src/runmux/web.py`, authenticated `GET /api/runs/history` (around line 127), forwarding to the existing bounded `RunStore.query_runs()` implementation in `store.py` (around line 447).
    - Representative backend cases: `modules/runmux/tests/historical_runs_api_test.py`, filter/identity tests around line 88, API allowlist/event cases around line 148, and 10,000-run bounded store query around line 224.
    
    ## Filter parameter schema
    
    The endpoint accepts query parameters. `cursor`, `limit`, `sort_by`, and `sort_dir` are already implemented by the frontend. Existing UI filters are partial `name`, `status`, `since`, `until`, `time_field`, `failed_only`, and `lost_only`.
    
    | Query parameter | Accepted value and behavior | Empty/default behavior | UI representation |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `state` | Optional exact enum `active` or `terminal`. `active` covers pending/running/paused; `terminal` covers finished/failed/killed/lost. Anything else raises store `ValueError` and the HTTP route returns 400. | Omit when unset. | Select: Any state / Active / Terminal. Stable ID `history-state-filter` (distinct from the existing status-message element `#history-state`). |
    | `name_exact` | Optional boolean; meaningful with `name`. When true, `name` is case-insensitive equality; otherwise `name` is an escaped case-insensitive substring. | Omit/false when no name is supplied. Never send `name_exact=true` by itself. | Checkbox `history-name-exact` alongside the existing name input. |
    | `exit_code` | Optional integer equality against the stored SQLite INTEGER column. Negative and zero values are valid; do not use truthiness to omit zero. SQLite integer storage is signed 64-bit. | Omit when blank. Reject non-integer and out-of-storage-range input client-side. FastAPI rejects malformed integer query values with 422; validly typed queries reach the store. | Number input `history-exit-code-filter`, integer step; allow signed values. |
    | `restart_of` | Optional string equality against a run's explicit restart-parent Run ID. The store does not infer a relation or resolve a name. | Omit when blank after trimming. | Text input `history-restart-parent-filter`; accept a full explicit Run ID, with no name/command/timestamp inference. |
    | `duplicate_of` | Optional string equality against a run's explicit duplicate-parent Run ID. | Omit when blank after trimming. | Text input `history-duplicate-parent-filter`; accept a full explicit Run ID. |
    | `has_restarts` | Optional boolean. `true` returns runs with at least one direct restart child; `false` means no filter, not “must have no restarts.” | Omit unless checked. There is no API `has_restarts=false` filter. | Checkbox `history-has-restarts`. |
    | `failed_only` / `lost_only` | Existing booleans; backend rejects both true together with HTTP 400. `failed_only` includes status failed or finished with nonzero exit code; `lost_only` means status lost. | Both false unless corresponding preset is active. | Existing mutually exclusive Failures / LOST presets. |
    
    `restart_of` and `duplicate_of` currently have no additional store-level format validation; they are exact string matches. Trim surrounding input whitespace and omit an empty result, but do not infer or rewrite IDs. Do not invent an API filter for “has duplicates.” `include_total` remains false/omitted by default.
    
    ## Canonical filter and preset state
    
    Maintain one canonical object for effective server query values. Preset identity is UI state that must match its effective constraints:
    
    - `recent` clears all filters to defaults. It must not leave either preset boolean set after manual edits or Clear.
    - `completed` sets `status=finished`; that criterion is already visible in the status control.
    - `failures` sets `failed_only=true`, `lost_only=false`; `lost` sets the inverse. These remain visibly active if combined with compatible manual filters such as name/date/exact-name/exit code.
    - If a manual status/state edit conflicts with the active failures/LOST predicate (for example, failures + status=lost, or either preset + state=active), clear that preset boolean and its active button state. Compatible constraints may remain combined while the preset remains visibly active.
    - Applying a manual exact-name or other compatible criterion must not silently clear the active preset. Clearing all filters resets every query field, preset boolean, and active-button indication.
    - The two preset booleans are mutually exclusive. No UI path may send both true.
    - Normalize controls before comparing effective state. A submission that does not change normalized filters should not dispatch another history request.
    - Any effective server filter, sort, or page-size change resets the cursor stack and aborts/ignores older requests. The backend binds a cursor to the complete normalized filter set and sort; a mismatched cursor returns HTTP 400.
    
    Date controls stay as previously implemented; do not change their meaning. Sort values remain `created_at`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `name`, or `numeric_id`, with direction `asc`/`desc`; limit remains 50/100/200 in the UI (API accepts 1–200).
    
    ## Pagination mutation semantics for D4
    
    The backend cursor is keyset pagination and captures an upper `(created_at, id)` boundary on the first page, preventing later/newer inserts from appearing in subsequent pages. It does not provide a full cross-request snapshot: deletes or updates that change filter membership can cause later pages to omit or shift records. D4 must test and document this behavior; it must not assert snapshot isolation.

Reuse this; do not add a new test framework.\n11: - Existing live-browser tests: `modules/runmux/tests/browser_e2e_test.js`, Phase 6C section beginning around line 530; viewport loop around line 850.\n12: - API contract: `modules/runmux/src/runmux/web.py`, authenticated `GET /api/runs/history` (around line 127), forwarding to the existing bounded `RunStore.query_runs()` implementation in `store.py` (around line 447).\n13: - Representative backend cases: `modules/runmux/tests/historical_runs_api_test.py`, filter/identity tests around line 88, API allowlist/event cases around line 148, and 10,000-run bounded store query around line 224.\n14: \n15: ## Filter parameter schema\n16: \n17: The endpoint accepts query parameters. `cursor`, `limit`, `sort_by`, and `sort_dir` are already implemented by the frontend. Existing UI filters are partial `name`, `status`, `since`, `until`, `time_field`, `failed_only`, and `lost_only`.\n18: \n19: | Query parameter | Accepted value and behavior | Empty/default behavior | UI representation |\n20: |---|---|---|---|\n21: | `state` | Optional exact enum `active` or `terminal`. `active` covers pending/running/paused; `terminal` covers finished/failed/killed/lost. Anything else raises store `ValueError` and the HTTP route returns 400. | Omit when unset. | Select: Any state / Active / Terminal. Stable ID `history-state-filter` (distinct from the existing status-message element `#history-state`). |\n22: | `name_exact` | Optional boolean; meaningful with `name`. When true, `name` is case-insensitive equality; otherwise `name` is an escaped case-insensitive substring. | Omit/false when no name is supplied. Never send `name_exact=true` by itself. | Checkbox `history-name-exact` alongside the existing name input. |\n23: | `exit_code` | Optional integer equality against the stored SQLite INTEGER column. Negative and zero values are valid; do not use truthiness to omit zero. SQLite integer storage is signed 64-bit. | Omit when blank. Reject non-integer and out-of-storage-range input client-side. FastAPI rejects malformed integer query values with 422; validly typed queries reach the store. | Number input `history-exit-code-filter`, integer step; allow signed values. |\n24: | `restart_of` | Optional string equality against a run's explicit restart-parent Run ID. The store does not infer a relation or resolve a name. | Omit when blank after trimming. | Text input `history-restart-parent-filter`; accept a full explicit Run ID, with no name/command/timestamp inference. |\n25: | `duplicate_of` | Optional string equality against a run's explicit duplicate-parent Run ID. | Omit when blank after trimming. | Text input `history-duplicate-parent-filter`; accept a full explicit Run ID. |\n26: | `has_restarts` | Optional boolean. `true` returns runs with at least one direct restart child; `false` means no filter, not “must have no restarts.” | Omit unless checked. There is no API `has_restarts=false` filter. | Checkbox `history-has-restarts`. |\n27: | `failed_only` / `lost_only` | Existing booleans; backend rejects both true together with HTTP 400. `failed_only` includes status failed or finished with nonzero exit code; `lost_only` means status lost. | Both false unless corresponding preset is active. | Existing mutually exclusive Failures / LOST presets. |\n28: \n29: `restart_of` and `duplicate_of` currently have no additional store-level format validation; they are exact string matches. Trim surrounding input whitespace and omit an empty result, but do not infer or rewrite IDs. Do not invent an API filter for “has duplicates.” `include_total` remains false/omitted by default.\n30: \n31: ## Canonical filter and preset state\n32: \n33: Maintain one canonical object for effective server query values. Preset identity is UI state that must match its effective constraints:\n34: \n35: - `recent` clears all filters to defaults. It must not leave either preset boolean set after manual edits or Clear.\n36: - `completed` sets `status=finished`; that criterion is already visible in the status control.\n37: - `failures` sets `failed_only=true`, `lost_only=false`; `lost` sets the inverse. These remain visibly active if combined with compatible manual filters such as name/date/exact-name/exit code.\n38: - If a manual status/state edit conflicts with the active failures/LOST predicate (for example, failures + status=lost, or either preset + state=active), clear that preset boolean and its active button state. Compatible constraints may remain combined while the preset remains visibly active.\n39: - Applying a manual exact-name or other compatible criterion must not silently clear the active preset. Clearing all filters resets every query field, preset boolean, and active-button indication.\n40: - The two preset booleans are mutually exclusive. No UI path may send both true.\n41: - Normalize controls before comparing effective state. A submission that does not change normalized filters should not dispatch another history request.\n42: - Any effective server filter, sort, or page-size change resets the cursor stack and aborts/ignores older requests. The backend binds a cursor to the complete normalized filter set and sort; a mismatched cursor returns HTTP 400.\n43: \n44: Date controls stay as previously implemented; do not change their meaning. Sort values remain `created_at`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `name`, or `numeric_id`, with direction `asc`/`desc`; limit remains 50/100/200 in the UI (API accepts 1–200).\n45: \n46: ## Pagination mutation semantics for D4\n47: \n48: The backend cursor is keyset pagination and captures an upper `(created_at, id)` boundary on the first page, preventing later/newer inserts from appearing in subsequent pages. It does not provide a full cross-request snapshot: deletes or updates that change filter membership can cause later pages to omit or shift records. D4 must test and document this behavior; it must not assert snapshot isolation.\n\n(End of file - total 48 lines)\n</content>\n\n<system-reminder>\nInstructions from: C:\\Users\\mcarls\\src\\scripts\\.worktrees\\runmux-6c-history-frontend-local-pilot\\modules\\runmux\\docs\\AGENTS.md\n# Runmux documentation instruction redirect\r\n\r\nRunmux-specific agent guidance now lives in [../AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md), at the module root.
