Reuse this; do not add a new test framework.\n- Existing live-browser tests: `modules/runmux/tests/browser_e2e_test.js`, Phase 6C section beginning around line 530; viewport loop around line 850.\n- API contract: `modules/runmux/src/runmux/web.py`, authenticated `GET /api/runs/history` (around line 127), forwarding to the existing bounded `RunStore.query_runs()` implementation in `store.py` (around line 447).\n- Representative backend cases: `modules/runmux/tests/historical_runs_api_test.py`, filter/identity tests around line 88, API allowlist/event cases around line 148, and 10,000-run bounded store query around line 224.\n\n## Filter parameter schema\n\nThe endpoint accepts query parameters. `cursor`, `limit`, `sort_by`, and `sort_dir` are already implemented by the frontend. Existing UI filters are partial `name`, `status`, `since`, `until`, `time_field`, `failed_only`, and `lost_only`.\n\n| Query parameter | Accepted value and behavior | Empty/default behavior | UI representation |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `state` | Optional exact enum `active` or `terminal`. `active` covers pending/running/paused; `terminal` covers finished/failed/killed/lost. Anything else raises store `ValueError` and the HTTP route returns 400. | Omit when unset. | Select: Any state / Active / Terminal. Stable ID `history-state-filter` (distinct from the existing status-message element `#history-state`). |\n| `name_exact` | Optional boolean; meaningful with `name`. When true, `name` is case-insensitive equality; otherwise `name` is an escaped case-insensitive substring. | Omit/false when no name is supplied. Never send `name_exact=true` by itself. | Checkbox `history-name-exact` alongside the existing name input. |\n| `exit_code` | Optional integer equality against the stored SQLite INTEGER column. Negative and zero values are valid; do not use truthiness to omit zero. SQLite integer storage is signed 64-bit. | Omit when blank. Reject non-integer and out-of-storage-range input client-side. FastAPI rejects malformed integer query values with 422; validly typed queries reach the store. | Number input `history-exit-code-filter`, integer step; allow signed values. |\n| `restart_of` | Optional string equality against a run's explicit restart-parent Run ID. The store does not infer a relation or resolve a name. | Omit when blank after trimming. | Text input `history-restart-parent-filter`; accept a full explicit Run ID, with no name/command/timestamp inference. |\n| `duplicate_of` | Optional string equality against a run's explicit duplicate-parent Run ID. | Omit when blank after trimming. | Text input `history-duplicate-parent-filter`; accept a full explicit Run ID. |\n| `has_restarts` | Optional boolean. `true` returns runs with at least one direct restart child; `false` means no filter, not “must have no restarts.” | Omit unless checked. There is no API `has_restarts=false` filter. | Checkbox `history-has-restarts`. |\n| `failed_only` / `lost_only` | Existing booleans; backend rejects both true together with HTTP 400. `failed_only` includes status failed or finished with nonzero exit code; `lost_only` means status lost. | Both false unless corresponding preset is active. | Existing mutually exclusive Failures / LOST presets. |\n\n`restart_of` and `duplicate_of` currently have no additional store-level format validation; they are exact string matches. Trim surrounding input whitespace and omit an empty result, but do not infer or rewrite IDs. Do not invent an API filter for “has duplicates.” `include_total` remains false/omitted by default.\n\n## Canonical filter and preset state\n\nMaintain one canonical object for effective server query values. Preset identity is UI state that must match its effective constraints:\n\n- `recent` clears all filters to defaults. It must not leave either preset boolean set after manual edits or Clear.\n- `completed` sets `status=finished`; that criterion is already visible in the status control.\n- `failures` sets `failed_only=true`, `lost_only=false`; `lost` sets the inverse. These remain visibly active if combined with compatible manual filters such as name/date/exact-name/exit code.\n- If a manual status/state edit conflicts with the active failures/LOST predicate (for example, failures + status=lost, or either preset + state=active), clear that preset boolean and its active button state. Compatible constraints may remain combined while the preset remains visibly active.\n- Applying a manual exact-name or other compatible criterion must not silently clear the active preset. Clearing all filters resets every query field, preset boolean, and active-button indication.\n- The two preset booleans are mutually exclusive. No UI path may send both true.\n- Normalize controls before comparing effective state. A submission that does not change normalized filters should not dispatch another history request.\n- Any effective server filter, sort, or page-size change resets the cursor stack and aborts/ignores older requests. The backend binds a cursor to the complete normalized filter set and sort; a mismatched cursor returns HTTP 400.\n\nDate controls stay as previously implemented; do not change their meaning. Sort values remain `created_at`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `name`, or `numeric_id`, with direction `asc`/`desc`; limit remains 50/100/200 in the UI (API accepts 1–200).\n\n## Pagination mutation semantics for D4\n\nThe backend cursor is keyset pagination and captures an upper `(created_at, id)` boundary on the first page, preventing later/newer inserts from appearing in subsequent pages. It does not provide a full cross-request snapshot: deletes or updates that change filter membership can cause later pages to omit or shift records. D4 must test and document this behavior; it must not assert snapshot isolation.","lineStart":1,"lineEnd":48,"totalLines":48,"truncated":false}},"title":"modules\\runmux\\docs\\plans\\20261024-1805_runmux-history-frontend-local-pilot\\D0-filter-contract.md","time":{"start":1792892900253,"end":1792892900259}},"id":"prt_170be91c7001C1KQXfpzNFjA4G","sessionID":"ses_e8f417354ffeh18PAswgGs4vIg","messageID":"msg_170be8cc2001baOg84jJULnqtT"},{"reason":"tool-calls","snapshot":"d6d868a53161e8b0d37aefdbba415fb9cb60a6e5","type":"step-finish","tokens":{"total":8648,"input":8540,"output":88,"reasoning":20,"cache":{"write":0,"read":0}},"cost":0,"id":"prt_170be944a001ZktqI61GKkKqDp","sessionID":"ses_e8f417354ffeh18PAswgGs4vIg","messageID":"msg_170be8cc2001baOg84jJULnqtT"}]},{"info":{"parentID":"msg_170be8ca0001a763610a8aa216","role":"assistant","mode":"local-worker","agent":"local-worker","path":{"cwd":"C:\\Users\\mcarls\\src\\scripts\\.worktrees\\runmux-6c-history-frontend-local-pilot","root":"C:\\Users\\mcarls\\src\\scripts\\.worktrees\\runmux-6c-history-frontend-local-pilot"},"cost":0,"tokens":{"total":11090,"input":10865,"output":202,"reasoning":23,"cache":{"write":0,"read":0}},"modelID":"qwen38_23GB","providerID":"lmstudio","time":{"created":1792892900578,"completed":1792892903469},"finish":"tool-calls","id":"msg_170be94e2001wqIPxCArz5juFi","sessionID":"ses_e8f417354ffeh18PAswgGs4vIg"},"parts":[{"snapshot":"d6d868a53161e8b0d37aefdbba415fb9cb60a6e5","type":"step-start","id":"prt_170be9934001GgpPDGt9R9nW2a","sessionID":"ses_e8f417354ffeh18PAswgGs4vIg","messageID":"msg_170be94e2001wqIPxCArz5juFi"},{"type":"reasoning","text":"Let     ---
    name: local-agent-handoff
    description: Use when coordinating repository work in Codex or Antigravity and a bounded exploration, review, draft, or implementation task can be delegated to the connected LM Studio worker through opencode_worker.
    ---
    
    # Local agent handoff
    
    Give the local worker a task it can complete and the coordinator can verify.
    Use it proactively for suitable subtasks within the user's authorized work.
    An instruction disabling delegation takes precedence. If you are the delegated
    worker rather than the coordinator, carry out your assigned task directly.
    
    ## Choose and prepare the task
    
    Good tasks include exploring a bounded set of files, a focused review, drafting
    tests or documentation, and a small edit with clear acceptance criteria. Keep tiny
    tasks in the coordinator when composing and reviewing a handoff would cost more
    than completing them. Resolve requirements and architectural choices first.
    
    Use the tools actually exposed by `opencode_worker`; this connection is not a native
    Codex/agy subagent. On first use or reconnection, use `opencode_setup` and, if needed,
    `opencode_context` with the absolute project `directory` to confirm readiness, the
    local provider/model and available agents. Reuse confirmed facts within the task.
    If the bridge is unavailable, continue locally or report the gap.
    Installing tools or changing bridge settings is separate work.
    
    Send the objective, absolute workspace, relevant context/instructions, allowed work,
    exclusions, checks and expected result. Use the
    [task envelope](references/task-envelope.md) when composing a handoff.
    Give file paths and targeted context so the worker can inspect source directly;
    do not copy the parent conversation or entire repository into the handoff.
    For shared checkouts, let only one actor edit overlapping paths. Give parallel
    writers separate worktrees before dispatch; a session is not filesystem isolation.
    
    ## Dispatch and continue
    
    Select the intended local provider/model, explicit `directory` and verified worker
    agent using the discovered tool schema. Never silently select a cloud fallback.
    Use `local-worker` for authorized edits or `local-reviewer` for inspection without
    edits or shell execution, after confirming the chosen agent exists. Both can use the bundled
    [worker prompt](resources/local-worker.md); its presence in this folder does not
    make it active in OpenCode.
    
    For coding work, prefer `opencode_fire` followed by `opencode_check` or bounded
    `opencode_wait` calls. Keep the returned `jobId`, `sessionId`, `messageId` and
    directory. Observe by job ID so an earlier session response cannot satisfy a new task.
    Keep waits shorter than the client's tool timeout. Codex documents a 60-second
    default; the pinned bridge's `opencode_run` defaults to a 600-second observation.
    For a short synchronous run, set `maxDurationSeconds` explicitly within that budget.
    
    Use a fresh session for an unrelated task and the original session for a related
    follow-up. A follow-up is new work with a new job ID; a timeout resumes observation
    of the existing job. Never resubmit work just because a wait expired.
    
    For delayed responses, required input or failures, read
    [results and recovery](references/results-and-recovery.md). Respect existing task
    authority when handling requests for more access or a missing decision.
    
    ## Review the result
    
    Fetch compact progress with `opencode_check` (`detailed: false`). Read full
    conversation history only to investigate missing evidence or a failure.
    Check the requested deliverable, supporting evidence, changed paths and reported
    validation. Inspect relevant source/diffs and run appropriate focused checks before
    integration. A completed tool response does not establish that the work is correct.
    
    If the worker cannot make progress, narrow the task or finish it locally. Preserve
    its useful evidence and report unresolved work instead of repeating blind retries.
    The coordinator remains responsible for integration and the final user response.

    # Web UI Development with Visual Iteration
    
    ## Overview
    
    This skill enables pixel-accurate visual iteration on web UI changes. Instead of
    working blind, take browser screenshots after every change, evaluate them against
    the design system, and adjust autonomously. The result is faster, higher-quality
    frontend work without constant user review of cosmetic details.
    
    ## Prerequisites
    
    Before starting any web UI work:
    
    1. **Start the dev server** with hot-reload. Try in order:
       ```bash
       webui -r -v -p 3001                    # If webui CLI is installed
       koweb -r -v -p 3001                    # Legacy alias
       cd ~/scripts/modules/web_ui_tools && uvicorn web_ui_tools.app:create_app --reload --port 3001
       ```
       If none of these commands are available, ask the user how to start their
       development server and on which port.
    
    2. **Take a baseline screenshot** of the current state before making any changes.
       This enables before/after comparison.
    
    3. **Load Playwright tools** via ToolSearch for `playwright` to enable browser
       screenshot capabilities.
    
    ## Core Workflow: Edit-Screenshot-Evaluate Loop
    
    For every visual change (CSS, HTML, layout, color, spacing, typography):
    
    ### 1. Make the Change
    Edit the file (CSS, HTML, JS, template).
    
    ### 2. Take a Screenshot
    Navigate to the relevant page and capture:
    
    ```
    browser_navigate → http://localhost:3001
    browser_take_screenshot
    ```
    
    For specific views or states, navigate to the appropriate route first.
    
    ### 3. Evaluate Against Design System
    Compare the screenshot to the design system defined in
    `references/design-system.md`. Check:
    
    - Color usage matches the defined palette
    - Typography uses the correct font families and sizes
    - Spacing follows the 4px/8px grid
    - Metric cards follow the panel pattern
    - Layout respects the grid structure
    - Contrast ratios are sufficient for readability
    - Real-time data elements have appropriate update indicators
    
    ### 4. Adjust or Approve
    If the result does not match the design system or looks visually wrong:
    - Make the adjustment
    - Re-screenshot
    - Re-evaluate
    - Repeat until satisfactory
    
    If the result matches the design system and looks clean, move to the next change.
    
    **Do NOT ask the user for approval on individual visual tweaks.** The design
    system is the authority. Only escalate to the user when:
    - A design system rule conflicts with functionality
    - The change fundamentally alters the page layout or information hierarchy
    - Multiple valid approaches exist with meaningfully different aesthetics
    
    ## Screenshot Techniques
    
    ### Full Page Capture
    ```
    browser_navigate → target URL
    browser_take_screenshot
    ```
    
    ### Responsive Testing
    ```
    browser_resize → width: 1920, height: 1080  (desktop)
    browser_take_screenshot
    browser_resize → width: 1366, height: 768   (laptop)
    browser_take_screenshot
    browser_resize → width: 768, height: 1024   (tablet)
    browser_take_screenshot
    ```
    
    ### Component Isolation
    To evaluate a specific component, use the browser snapshot tool to identify
    the element, then evaluate its rendered appearance in the full screenshot.
    
    ### Dark Theme Verification
    The UI is dark-theme-only. Verify that:
    - Text is readable against dark backgrounds
    - Panel borders are subtle but visible
    - Active/hover states are distinguishable
    - Status colors pop against the dark canvas
    
    ## What "Good" Looks Like
    
    ### Metric Cards
    - Large numeric value (24-32px, bold, white)
    - Small label below (12px, muted gray)
    - Optional sparkline in top-right corner
    - Subtle border or background differentiation from canvas
    - Consistent padding (16px internal)
    
    ### Data Tables
    - Header row with muted text, no heavy borders
    - Alternating row backgrounds (subtle, 2-3% opacity difference)
    - Sortable columns indicated by caret icons
    - Monospace font for numeric data
    - Status badges with appropriate colors
    
    ### Live Feeds
    - Newest items at top
    - Timestamp in muted color
    - Event type badges with semantic colors
    - Smooth entry animation (fade-in or slide)
    - Auto-scroll with pause-on-hover
    
    ### Overall Layout
    - Fixed sidebar or top nav (not both)
    - Content area uses CSS Grid for panel arrangement
    - Panels have consistent border-radius (8px)
    - Spacing between panels: 16px gap
    - No horizontal scroll at 1366px+
    
    ## Additional Resources
    
    ### Reference Files
    
    Consult these for detailed specifications:
    
    - **`references/design-system.md`** - Complete color palette, typography scale,
      spacing system, component specifications, and CSS variable definitions
    - **`references/visual-qa-checklist.md`** - Step-by-step checklist to run after
      completing a visual change, covering accessibility, responsiveness, and polish
    
    ### Using the local-web Skill
    
    If Playwright MCP is unavailable, invoke the `local-web` skill as an
    alternative for accessing local development servers and taking screenshots.
    
    ## Anti-Patterns
    
    - **Working blind**: Never make more than 2-3 CSS changes without screenshotting
    - **Asking for color opinions**: The design system defines the palette; use it
    - **Ignoring contrast**: Always verify text readability on dark backgrounds
    - **Pixel-pushing without context**: Check the full page, not just the edited component
    - **Forgetting responsive**: Test at least desktop (1920) and laptop (1366) widths

    ## Filter parameter schema
    
    The endpoint accepts query parameters. `cursor`, `limit`, `sort_by`, and `sort_dir` are already implemented by the frontend. Existing UI filters are partial `name`, `status`, `since`, `until`, `time_field`, `failed_only`, and `lost_only`.
    
    | Query parameter | Accepted value and behavior | Empty/default behavior | UI representation |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `state` | Optional exact enum `active` or `terminal`. `active` covers pending/running/paused; `terminal` covers finished/failed/killed/lost. Anything else raises store `ValueError` and the HTTP route returns 400. | Omit when unset. | Select: Any state / Active / Terminal. Stable ID `history-state-filter` (distinct from the existing status-message element `#history-state`). |
    | `name_exact` | Optional boolean; meaningful with `name`. When true, `name` is case-insensitive equality; otherwise `name` is an escaped case-insensitive substring. | Omit/false when no name is supplied. Never send `name_exact=true` by itself. | Checkbox `history-name-exact` alongside the existing name input. |
    | `exit_code` | Optional integer equality against the stored SQLite INTEGER column. Negative and zero values are valid; do not use truthiness to omit zero. SQLite integer storage is signed 64-bit. | Omit when blank. Reject non-integer and out-of-storage-range input client-side. FastAPI rejects malformed integer query values with 422; validly typed queries reach the store. | Number input `history-exit-code-filter`, integer step; allow signed values. |
    | `restart_of` | Optional string equality against a run's explicit restart-parent Run ID. The store does not infer a relation or resolve a name. | Omit when blank after trimming. | Text input `history-restart-parent-filter`; accept a full explicit Run ID, with no name/command/timestamp inference. |
    | `duplicate_of` | Optional string equality against a run's explicit duplicate-parent Run ID. | Omit when blank after trimming. | Text input `history-duplicate-parent-filter`; accept a full explicit Run ID. |
    | `has_restarts` | Optional boolean. `true` returns runs with at least one direct restart child; `false` means no filter, not “must have no restarts.” | Omit unless checked. There is no API `has_restarts=false` filter. | Checkbox `history-has-restarts`. |
    | `failed_only` / `lost_only` | Existing booleans; backend rejects both true together with HTTP 400. `failed_only` includes status failed or finished with nonzero exit code; `lost_only` means status lost. | Both false unless corresponding preset is active. | Existing mutually exclusive Failures / LOST presets. |
    
    `restart_of` and `duplicate_of` currently have no additional store-level format validation; they are exact string matches. Trim surrounding input whitespace and omit an empty result, but do not infer or rewrite IDs. Do not invent an API filter for “has duplicates.” `include_total` remains false/omitted by default.
    
    ## Canonical filter and preset state
    
    Maintain one canonical object for effective server query values. Preset identity is UI state that must match its effective constraints:
    
    - `recent` clears all filters to defaults. It must not leave either preset boolean set after manual edits or Clear.
    - `completed` sets `status=finished`; that criterion is already visible in the status control.
    - `failures` sets `failed_only=true`, `lost_only=false`; `lost` sets the inverse. These remain visibly active if combined with compatible manual filters such as name/date/exact-name/exit code.
    - If a manual status/state edit conflicts with the active failures/LOST predicate (for example, failures + status=lost, or either preset + state=active), clear that preset boolean and its active button state. Compatible constraints may remain combined while the preset remains visibly active.
    - Applying a manual exact-name or other compatible criterion must not silently clear the active preset. Clearing all filters resets every query field, preset boolean, and active-button indication.
    - The two preset booleans are mutually exclusive. No UI path may send both true.
    - Normalize controls before comparing effective state. A submission that does not change normalized filters should not dispatch another history request.
    - Any effective server filter, sort, or page-size change resets the cursor stack and aborts/ignores older requests. The backend binds a cursor to the complete normalized filter set and sort; a mismatched cursor returns HTTP 400.
    
    Date controls stay as previously implemented; do not change their meaning. Sort values remain `created_at`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `name`, or `numeric_id`, with direction `asc`/`desc`; limit remains 50/100/200 in the UI (API accepts 1–200).
    
    ## Pagination mutation semantics for D4
    
    The backend cursor is keyset pagination and captures an upper `(created_at, id)` boundary on the first page, preventing later/newer inserts from appearing in subsequent pages. It does not provide a full cross-request snapshot: deletes or updates that change filter membership can cause later pages to omit or shift records. D4 must test and document this behavior; it must not assert snapshot isolation.

      runHistoryAbortController = new AbortController();
      runHistoryBusy = true;
      runHistoryError = "";
      renderHistoryPage();

        const response = await api(runHistoryQueryUrl(), { signal: runHistoryAbortController.signal });

        runHistoryItems = Array.isArray(result.items) ? result.items.slice(0, RUN_HISTORY_PAGE_MAX) : [];
        runHistoryHasMore = result.has_more === true;
        if (runHistoryHasMore && typeof result.next_cursor === "string" && result.next_cursor) {
          runHistoryPageCursors[runHistoryPageIndex + 1] = result.next_cursor;
        } else {
          runHistoryPageCursors.length = runHistoryPageIndex + 1;
          runHistoryHasMore = false;
        }
      } catch (error) {
        if (generation !== runHistoryRequestGeneration || error.name === "AbortError") return;
        if (error.message === "locked") { showLogin("Session expired. Enter the current terminal login code again."); return; }

          ? `History filters were rejected: ${error.message}`

            ? "Historical registry is temporarily unavailable. Try again."

      }
    }

      if (name === "time_field" && !["created_at", "started_at", "ended_at"].includes(value)) return Promise.resolve();

      assert.equal(requests.length, beforeClose, "Closing the history view must not dispatch any process lifecycle request");
    }
    
    async function testHistoricalExplorerSendsSupportedDateAndSortFilters() {
      const { context, requests } = dashboardHarness();
      const db = context.__dashboard;
      const opening = db.openHistoryView();
      await Promise.resolve();
      requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/api/runs/history")).resolve(response({ items: [], has_more: false }));
      await opening;
      const filtered = db.setHistoryFilter("since", "2026-10-24");
      await Promise.resolve();
      const request = requests.filter((item) => item.url.includes("/api/runs/history")).at(-1);
      assert.match(request.url, /since=2026-10-24T/);
      assert.match(request.url, /time_field=created_at/);
      request.resolve(response({ items: [], has_more: false }));
      await filtered;
      const sorted = db.setHistoryFilter("sort_by", "ended_at");
      await Promise.resolve();
      const sortRequest = requests.filter((item) => item.url.includes("/api/runs/history")).at(-1);
      assert.match(sortRequest.url, /sort_by=ended_at/);
      sortRequest.resolve(response({ items: [], has_more: false }));
      await sorted;
    }
    
    async function testHistoricalExplorerIgnoresObsoleteFilterResponses() {
      const { context, requests } = dashboardHarness();
      const db = context.__dashboard;
      const initial = db.openHistoryView();
      await Promise.resolve();
      const first = requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/api/runs/history"));
      const filtered = db.setHistoryFilter("name", "new query");
      await Promise.resolve();
      const second = requests.filter((request) => request.url.includes("/api/runs/history")).at(-1);
      assert.notEqual(first, second);
      assert.equal(first.options.signal.aborted, true, "Changing filters should abort an obsolete history request");
      assert.match(second.url, /name=new\+query|name=new%20query/);
      second.resolve(response({ items: [{ id: "fresh-id", name: "fresh", status: "lost" }], next_cursor: null, has_more: false, page_size: 1 }));
      await filtered;
      first.resolve(response({ items: [{ id: "stale-id", name: "stale", status: "finished" }], next_cursor: null, has_more: false, page_size: 1 }));
      await initial;
      assert.equal(db.historyState().items[0].id, "fresh-id");
    }
    
    async function testHistoricalExplorerReportsApiErrorsAndUnauthorizedSessions() {
      const failed = dashboardHarness();
      const failedDb = failed.context.__dashboard;
      const failureLoad = failedDb.openHistoryView();
      await Promise.resolve();
      failed.requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/api/runs/history")).resolve(response({ detail: "bad sort key" }, 400));
      await failureLoad;
      assert.match(failed.getElement("#history-state").textContent, /filters were rejected/i);
    
      const unauthorized = dashboardHarness();
      const unauthorizedLoad = unauthorized.context.__dashboard.openHistoryView();
      await Promise.resolve();
      unauthorized.requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/api/runs/history")).resolve(response({ detail: "expired" }, 401));
      await unauthorizedLoad;
      assert.equal(unauthorized.getElement("#dashboard").hidden, true);
      assert.match(unauthorized.getElement("#login-error").textContent, /session expired/i);
    }
    
    async function testRunDetailsShowEventProvenanceAndExplicitLineage() {
      const { context, requests, getElement } = dashboardHarness();
      const db = context.__dashboard;
      db.setSelectedId("run-current");
      const details = db.refreshRunHistoryDetails("run-current");
      await Promise.resolve();
      const eventsRequest = requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/events?"));
      const lineageRequest = requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/lineage?"));
      assert.match(eventsRequest.url, /limit=100/);
      assert.match(lineageRequest.url, /limit=200/);
      eventsRequest.resolve(response({ run_id: "run-current", has_more: false, events: [
        { event_type: "pause", timestamp: "2026-10-24T10:00:00Z", provenance: "telemetry_store", reason: "private reason" },
        { event_type: "registered", timestamp: "2026-10-24T09:00:00Z", provenance: "registry_record", related_run_id: "run-parent" },
      ] }));
      lineageRequest.resolve(response({ run_id: "run-current", root_run_id: "run-parent", ancestors: [
        { id: "run-parent", name: "same name", status: "finished", created_at: "2026-10-24T08:00:00Z", relationship: "parent_restart" },
      ], descendants: [{ id: "run-child", name: "same name", status: "failed", created_at: "2026-10-24T11:00:00Z", relationship: "child_duplicate" }], truncated: false }));
      await details;
      const eventsText = getElement("#run-events-list").textContent;
      assert.match(eventsText, /Recorded event/);
      assert.match(eventsText, /Registry timestamp/);
      assert.doesNotMatch(eventsText, /private reason/);
      assert.match(getElement("#run-lineage-list").textContent, /Restarted from: same name · run-parent/);
      assert.match(getElement("#run-lineage-list").textContent, /Duplicated by: same name · run-child/);
    }
    
    async function testRunDetailsRepresentMissingEventsAndLineageHonestly() {
      const { context, requests, getElement } = dashboardHarness();
      const db = context.__dashboard;
      db.setSelectedId("orphan-run");
      const details = db.refreshRunHistoryDetails("orphan-run");
      await Promise.resolve();
      requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/events?")).resolve(response({ events: [], has_more: false }));
      requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/lineage?")).resolve(response({ ancestors: [], descendants: [], truncated: false }));
      await details;
      assert.match(getElement("#run-events-state").textContent, /no lifecycle events or registry timestamp markers/i);
      assert.match(getElement("#run-lineage-state").textContent, /no recorded restart or duplicate relationships/i);
    }
    
    async function testRunDetailsReportMissingRunsAndApiFailures() {
      const { context, requests, getElement } = dashboardHarness();
      const db = context.__dashboard;
      db.setSelectedId("removed-run");
      const details = db.refreshRunHistoryDetails("removed-run");
      await Promise.resolve();
      requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/events?")).resolve(response({ detail: "Run not found" }, 404));
      requests.find((request) => request.url.includes("/lineage?")).resolve(response({ detail: "registry unavailable" }, 503));
      await details;
      assert.match(getElement("#run-events-state").textContent, /no longer present in the registry/i);
      assert.match(getElement("#run-lineage-state").textContent, /temporarily unavailable/i);
    }

    [build-system]
    requires = ["hatchling>=1.24"]
    build-backend = "hatchling.build"
    
    [project]
    name = "runmux"
    version = "0.14.0"
    description = "Cross-platform managed process runner with shared live view and interaction sessions."
    readme = "README.md"
    requires-python = ">=3.10"
    license = { text = "MIT" }
    authors = [
        { name = "Max" }
    ]
    keywords = [
        "cli",
        "process-manager",
        "pty",
        "terminal",
        "powershell",
        "windows",
        "linux"
    ]
    classifiers = [
        "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",
        "Environment :: Console",
        "Intended Audience :: Developers",
        "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
        "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
        "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
        "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
        "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
        "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
        "Topic :: System :: Monitoring",
        "Topic :: Terminals"
    ]
    dependencies = [
        "psutil>=5.9",
        "resource-metrics>=0.1.0",
        "pywinpty>=3.0.0; sys_platform == 'win32'",
    ]
    
    [project.optional-dependencies]
    tui = [
        "cli_tui>=0.2.1",
        "windows-curses>=2.4; sys_platform == 'win32'",
    ]
    web = ["web-ui-tools>=0.1.0"]
    dev = [
        "pytest>=8.0",
        "ruff>=0.6"
    ]
    
    [project.scripts]
    runmux = "runmux.cli:main"
    
    [tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
    packages = ["src/runmux"]
    include = ["src/runmux/web_static/**"]
    
    [tool.pytest.ini_options]
    testpaths = ["tests"]
    addopts = "-q --basetemp=.pytest_tmp_root"
    
    [tool.ruff]
    line-length = 120
    target-version = "py310"
    
    [tool.ruff.lint]
    select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "SIM"]
    ignore = []

          def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
            attrs=dict(attrs)
            if attrs.get('id'): self.ids[attrs['id']]=self.ids.get(attrs['id'],0)+1
            if tag=='label':
              label={'for':attrs.get('for'),'controls':[]}; self.labels.append(label); self.stack.append(label)
            if tag in ('input','select','textarea'):
              for label in self.stack: label['controls'].append(attrs.get('id'))
          def handle_endtag(self, tag):
            if tag=='label' and self.stack: self.stack.pop()

    # Test-Driven Development (TDD)
    
    ## Overview
    
    Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.
    
    **Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.
    
    **Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**
    
    ## When to Use
    
    **Always:**
    - New features
    - Bug fixes
    - Refactoring
    - Behavior changes
    
    **Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
    - Throwaway prototypes
    - Generated code
    - Configuration files
    
    Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.
    
    ## The Iron Law
    
    ```
    NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
    ```
    
    Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.
    
    **No exceptions:**
    - Don't keep it as "reference"
    - Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
    - Don't look at it
    - Delete means delete
    
    Implement fresh from tests. Period.
    
    ## Red-Green-Refactor
    
    ```dot
    digraph tdd_cycle {
        rankdir=LR;
        red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
        verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
        green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
        verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
        refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
        next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];
    
        red -> verify_red;
        verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
        verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
        green -> verify_green;
        verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
        verify_green -> green [label="no"];
        refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
        verify_green -> next;
        next -> red;
    }
    ```
    
    ### RED - Write Failing Test
    
    Write one minimal test showing what should happen.
    
    <Good>
    ```typescript
    test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
      let attempts = 0;
      const operation = () => {
        attempts++;
        if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
        return 'success';
      };
    
      const result = await retryOperation(operation);
    
      expect(result).toBe('success');
      expect(attempts).toBe(3);
    });
    ```
    Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
    </Good>
    
    <Bad>
    ```typescript
    test('retry works', async () => {
      const mock = jest.fn()
        .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
        .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
        .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
      await retryOperation(mock);
      expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
    });
    ```
    Vague name, tests mock not code
    </Bad>
    
    **Requirements:**
    - One behavior
    - Clear name
    - Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)
    
    ### Verify RED - Watch It Fail
    
    **MANDATORY. Never skip.**
    
    ```bash
    npm test path/to/test.test.ts
    ```
    
    Confirm:
    - Test fails (not errors)
    - Failure message is expected
    - Fails because feature missing (not typos)
    
    **Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.
    
    **Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.
    
    ### GREEN - Minimal Code
    
    Write simplest code to pass the test.
    
    <Good>
    ```typescript
    async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
      for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
        try {
          return await fn();
        } catch (e) {
          if (i === 2) throw e;
        }
      }
      throw new Error('unreachable');
    }
    ```
    Just enough to pass
    </Good>
    
    <Bad>
    ```typescript
    async function retryOperation<T>(
      fn: () => Promise<T>,
      options?: {
        maxRetries?: number;
        backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
        onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
      }
    ): Promise<T> {
      // YAGNI
    }
    ```
    Over-engineered
    </Bad>
    
    Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.
    
    ### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass
    
    **MANDATORY.**
    
    ```bash
    npm test path/to/test.test.ts
    ```
    
    Confirm:
    - Test passes
    - Other tests still pass
    - Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
    
    **Test fails?** Fix code, not test.
    
    **Other tests fail?** Fix now.
    
    **"Other tests" means the project's suite, not just your file.** A
    green run of the test you wrote is not a green suite. Before you call
    the change done, run the project's test command (bare `pytest`,
    `npm test`, `cargo test` — whatever the repo uses) even when your task
    named only one test file. A scope statement in your task bounds the
    deliverable, not your verification. Any failure that run shows —
    including one you didn't cause — goes in your report by name; a red
    test you watched scroll past and didn't mention is a report falsified
    by omission.
    
    ### REFACTOR - Clean Up
    
    After green only:
    - Remove duplication
    - Improve names
    - Extract helpers
    
    Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.
    
    ### Repeat
    
    Next failing test for next feature.
    
    ## Good Tests
    
    | Quality | Good | Bad |
    |---------|------|-----|
    | **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
    | **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
    | **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |
    
    When writing or changing any test, read [writing-good-tests.md](writing-good-tests.md) for the rules that keep tests honest:
    - Name the production change that would make the test fail — before writing it
    - Assert on real behavior, never on mock behavior
    - Keep test-only code in test utilities, out of production classes
    - Understand a dependency's side effects before mocking it

    def _insert_run(
        store: RunStore,
        run_id: str,
        *,
        created_at: str,
        status: str = "finished",
        name: str | None = "sample",
        started_at: str | None = None,
        ended_at: str | None = None,
        exit_code: int | None = 0,
        restart_of: str | None = None,
        duplicate_of: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        with sqlite3.connect(store.db_path) as connection:
            connection.execute(
                """INSERT INTO runs (
                    id, numeric_id, name, status, created_at, updated_at, started_at, ended_at,
                    exit_code, pid, supervisor_pid, program, argv_json, cwd, env_overrides_json,
                    port, auth_token, log_path, command_line, restart_of, duplicate_of, rows, columns
                ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, NULL, NULL, ?, ?, ?, ?, NULL, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 24, 80)""",
                (
                    run_id,
                    int(run_id[-6:], 16),
                    name,
                    status,
                    created_at,
                    created_at,
                    started_at,
                    ended_at,
                    exit_code,
                    sys.executable,
                    "[]",
                    str(store.state_dir),
                    "{}",
                    "test-token",
                    str(store.state_dir / "secret-output.log"),
                    "secret command arguments",
                    restart_of,
                    duplicate_of,
                ),
            )
    
    
    def _record(store: RunStore, index: int) -> str:
        run_id = f"20261024-120000-{index:06x}"
        _insert_run(store, run_id, created_at="2026-10-24T12:00:00+00:00")
        return run_id
    
    
    def test_query_runs_keyset_is_stable_and_rejects_changed_filters(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        store = RunStore(tmp_path)
        created = "2026-10-24T12:00:00+00:00"
        ids = [f"20261024-120000-{index:06x}" for index in range(5)]
        for run_id in ids:
            _insert_run(store, run_id, created_at=created)
    
        first = store.query_runs(limit=2)
        assert [item.id for item in first.items] == sorted(ids, reverse=True)[:2]
        assert first.has_more is True
    
        _insert_run(store, "20261024-130000-000099", created_at="2026-10-24T13:00:00+00:00")
        second = store.query_runs(limit=2, cursor=first.next_cursor)
        assert [item.id for item in second.items] == sorted(ids, reverse=True)[2:4]
        assert second.has_more is True
    
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="filters do not match"):
            store.query_runs(limit=2, cursor=first.next_cursor, status="failed")
    
    
    def test_query_runs_filters_are_applied_in_sql_and_run_ids_remain_identity(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        store = RunStore(tmp_path)
        created = "2026-10-24T12:00:00+00:00"
        _insert_run(
            store, "20261024-120000-000001", created_at=created, ended_at=created, name="Same", status="failed", exit_code=2
        )
        _insert_run(
            store,
            "20261024-120000-000002",
            created_at=created,
            ended_at=created,
            name="Same",
            status="finished",
            exit_code=0,
        )
        _insert_run(
            store,
            "20261024-120000-000003",
            created_at=created,
            ended_at=created,
            name="Other",
            status="lost",
            exit_code=None,
        )
    
        page = store.query_runs(name="same", failed_only=True)
        assert [record.id for record in page.items] == ["20261024-120000-000001"]
        assert [record.id for record in store.query_runs(lost_only=True).items] == ["20261024-120000-000003"]
        assert store.query_runs(state="terminal", limit=1).page_size == 1
        bounded = store.query_runs(
            since="2026-10-24T12:00:00Z",
            until=1792843200,
            time_field="ended_at",
            name="same",
            sort_by="numeric_id",
            sort_dir="asc",
            include_total=True,
        )
        assert [record.id for record in bounded.items] == ["20261024-120000-000001", "20261024-120000-000002"]
        assert bounded.total_count == 2
    
    
    def test_lineage_uses_explicit_restart_and_duplicate_ids(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        store = RunStore(tmp_path)
        created = "2026-10-24T12:00:00+00:00"
        root = "20261024-120000-000001"
        restarted = "20261024-120001-000002"
        duplicate = "20261024-120002-000003"
        _insert_run(store, root, created_at=created)
        _insert_run(store, restarted, created_at=created, restart_of=root)
        _insert_run(store, duplicate, created_at=created, duplicate_of=root)
    
        lineage = store.get_run_lineage(root)
        assert lineage.root_run_id == root
        assert lineage.ancestors == []
        assert {node.id for node in lineage.descendants} == {restarted, duplicate}
        assert lineage.total_restarts == 1
        assert lineage.total_duplicates == 1
        restarted_lineage = store.get_run_lineage(restarted)
        assert [(node.id, node.relationship) for node in restarted_lineage.ancestors] == [(root, "parent_restart")]
    
    
    def test_history_adapter_and_routes_are_allowlisted_and_truthful(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        store = RunStore(tmp_path)
        run_id = "20261024-120000-000001"
        child_id = "20261024-120001-000002"
        created = "2026-10-24T12:00:00+00:00"
        _insert_run(store, run_id, created_at=created, status="finished", started_at=created, ended_at=created)
        _insert_run(store, child_id, created_at=created, status="running", restart_of=run_id)
        telemetry_store = TelemetryStore(tmp_path)
        telemetry_store.record_event(
            run_id,
            "pause",
            timestamp=1792843200.0,
            reason="secret reason",
            details={"token": "secret"},
        )
        telemetry_store.record_event(run_id, "resume", timestamp=1792843201.0)
        telemetry_store.record_event(run_id, "checkpoint", timestamp=1792843202.0)
    
        backend = ReadOnlyRunmux(tmp_path)
        payload = backend.query_runs_history(limit=1)
        assert payload["page_size"] == 1
        item = payload["items"][0]
        assert item["id"] in {run_id, child_id}
        assert not {"argv_json", "cwd", "env_overrides_json", "auth_token", "port", "log_path", "command_line"} & set(item)
    
        events = backend.get_run_events(run_id)
        event_rows = events["events"]
        assert {event["provenance"] for event in event_rows} == {"registry_record", "telemetry_store"}
        assert any(event["event_type"] == "pause" for event in event_rows)
        assert any(event["event_type"] == "restarted_by" and event["related_run_id"] == child_id for event in event_rows)
        assert all("secret" not in json.dumps(event).lower() for event in event_rows)
        first_event_page = backend.get_run_events(run_id, limit=2)
        assert first_event_page["has_more"] is True
        event_cursor = first_event_page["next_cursor"]
        all_event_pages = list(first_event_page["events"])
        while event_cursor:
            next_event_page = backend.get_run_events(run_id, limit=2, cursor=event_cursor)
            all_event_pages.extend(next_event_page["events"])
            event_cursor = next_event_page["next_cursor"]
        assert {event["event_type"] for event in all_event_pages} >= {"pause", "resume", "checkpoint"}
        assert len({(event["timestamp"], event["event_type"], event.get("event_id")) for event in all_event_pages}) == len(
            all_event_pages
        )
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="limit must be between"):
            backend.get_run_events(run_id, limit=0)
        lineage = backend.get_run_lineage(run_id)
        assert lineage["run_id"] == run_id
        assert lineage["descendants"][0]["id"] == child_id
    
        app = create_runmux_web_app(tmp_path, login_code="secret", enable_telemetry_history=False)
        paths = {route.path for route in app.routes}
        assert {"/api/runs", "/api/runs/history", "/api/runs/{run_id}/events", "/api/runs/{run_id}/lineage"} <= paths
    
    
    def test_history_adapter_rejects_invalid_cursor_and_unknown_run(tmp_path: Path) -> None:

    def test_ten_thousand_run_registry_queries_remain_page_bounded(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        store = RunStore(tmp_path)
        base = "2026-10-24T12:00:00+00:00"
        with sqlite3.connect(store.db_path) as connection:
            connection.executemany(
                """INSERT INTO runs (
                    id, numeric_id, name, status, created_at, updated_at, started_at, ended_at, exit_code,
                    program, argv_json, cwd, env_overrides_json, auth_token, log_path, command_line,
                    restart_of, duplicate_of, rows, columns
                ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, NULL, ?, ?, ?, '[]', '/', '{}', 'token', '/secret/path', 'cmd',
                    NULL, NULL, 24, 80)""",
                (
                    (
                        f"20261024-120000-{index:06x}",
                        index,
                        f"worker-{index % 100}",
                        "failed" if index % 10 == 0 else "finished",
                        f"2026-10-24T12:{index // 600:02d}:{(index // 10) % 60:02d}+00:00",
                        base,
                        base,
                        1 if index % 10 == 0 else 0,
                        sys.executable,
                    )
                    for index in range(10_000)
                ),

    """Integration tests for authenticated browser lifecycle API endpoints (Phase 4A)."""
    
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import json

    def create_test_run(
        store: RunStore,
        state_dir: Path,
        run_id: str = "20261024-010101-abcdef",
        status: str = "running",
        pid: int = 12345,
        supervisor_pid: int = 12346,
        port: int | None = 45123,
        argv: list[str] | None = None,
    ) -> RunRecord:
        run_dir = state_dir / "runs" / run_id
        run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        log_path = run_dir / "output.ansi"
        if not log_path.exists():
            log_path.write_bytes(b"")
    
        argv_json = json.dumps(argv or ["python", "worker.py"])
        store.create_run(
            run_id=run_id,
            name="test-worker",
            status=status,
            program="python",
            argv_json=argv_json,
            cwd=str(state_dir),
            env_overrides_json="{}",
            auth_token="test-secret",
            log_path=log_path,
            command_line="python worker.py",
        )
        return store.update_run(
            run_id,
            pid=pid,
            supervisor_pid=supervisor_pid,
            port=port,
            status=status,
        )
    
    
    def test_unauthenticated_lifecycle_requests_rejected(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        app = create_runmux_web_app(tmp_path, login_code="secret123")
        run_id = "20261024-010101-abcdef"
    
        with TestClient(app, base_url="http://localhost") as client:
            for action in ("stop", "kill", "restart", "duplicate", "pause", "resume"):
                res = client.post(f"/api/runs/{run_id}/{action}", headers={"Origin": "http://localhost"})
                assert res.status_code in {401, 403}
    
    
    def test_wrong_origin_lifecycle_requests_rejected(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        app = create_runmux_web_app(tmp_path, login_code="secret123")
        run_id = "20261024-010101-abcdef"
    
        with TestClient(app, base_url="http://localhost") as client:
            # Login with legitimate origin
            login_res = client.post("/auth/login", json={"code": "secret123"}, headers={"Origin": "http://localhost"})
            assert login_res.status_code == 204
    
            # Mutation request from evil origin must be rejected with 403
            for action in ("stop", "restart", "duplicate", "pause", "resume"):
                res = client.post(f"/api/runs/{run_id}/{action}", headers={"Origin": "http://evil.com"})
                assert res.status_code == 403
    
    
    def test_non_existent_and_invalid_run_ids_return_404(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        app = create_runmux_web_app(tmp_path, login_code="secret123")
    
        with TestClient(app, base_url="http://localhost") as client:
            client.post("/auth/login", json={"code": "secret123"}, headers={"Origin": "http://localhost"})
    
            # Valid format but non-existent run
            res = client.post("/api/runs/20261024-999999-000000/stop", headers={"Origin": "http://localhost"})
            assert res.status_code == 404
    
            # Invalid format (numeric ID or prefix)
            res_numeric = client.post("/api/runs/0/stop", headers={"Origin": "http://localhost"})

    def _terminal_status(value: dict[str, Any], *, mode: str, finished: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Project only attachment and input-lock state to the browser terminal."""
    
        return {
            "type": "status",
            "mode": mode,
            "session_holds_lock": bool(value.get("session_holds_lock")),
            "session_queue_position": value.get("session_queue_position"),
            "lock_queue_count": value.get("lock_queue_count", 0),
            "current_interactors": value.get("current_interactors", 0),
            "finished": finished,
        }
    
    
    def _close_input_channel(channel: Any | None) -> None:
        if channel is None:
            return
        with suppress(OSError):
            channel.shutdown(socket.SHUT_WR)
        with suppress(OSError):
            channel.close()

    def test_api_auth_listing_detail_and_safe_bounded_output(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        state_dir = tmp_path / "state"
        store = RunStore(state_dir)
        run_id = "20261023-123456-a1b2c3"
        make_run(store, state_dir, run_id)
        app = create_runmux_web_app(state_dir, login_code="test-login")
    
        with TestClient(app, base_url="http://localhost") as client:
            unauthorized = client.get("/api/runs", headers={"Origin": "http://localhost"})
            assert unauthorized.status_code == 401
            assert unauthorized.headers["cache-control"] == "no-store"
    
            login = client.post("/auth/login", json={"code": "test-login"}, headers={"Origin": "http://localhost"})
            assert login.status_code == 204
            assert "httponly" in login.headers["set-cookie"].lower()
    
            listing = client.get("/api/runs", headers={"Origin": "http://localhost"})
            assert listing.status_code == 200
            assert listing.headers["cache-control"] == "no-store"
            assert listing.json()[0]["id"] == run_id
            assert listing.json()[0]["command"] == "worker.exe"
            assert "command_line" not in listing.text
            assert "should-not-leak" not in listing.text
            assert "private\\folder" not in listing.text
            assert "ipc-secret" not in listing.text
            assert "env-secret" not in listing.text
    
            detail = client.get(f"/api/runs/{run_id}", headers={"Origin": "http://localhost"})
            assert detail.status_code == 200
            assert detail.json()["name"] == "sample worker"
            assert client.get("/api/runs/20261023-123", headers={"Origin": "http://localhost"}).status_code == 404
    
            output = client.get(f"/api/runs/{run_id}/output", headers={"Origin": "http://localhost"})
            assert output.status_code == 200
            assert output.json()["text"] == "line <script>alert(1)</script>\n"
            assert "\x1b" not in output.json()["text"]
            assert output.headers["cache-control"] == "no-store"
    
            assert client.get("/api/runs", headers={"Origin": "http://attacker.invalid"}).status_code == 403
            invalid_cursor = client.get(
                f"/api/runs/{run_id}/output?cursor=invalid",
                headers={"Origin": "http://localhost"},
            )
            assert invalid_cursor.status_code == 400
    
    
    def test_missing_registry_stays_empty_without_creating_it(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
        state_dir = tmp_path / "missing-registry"
        app = create_runmux_web_app(state_dir, login_code="test-login")
        with TestClient(app, base_url="http://localhost") as client:
            client.post("/auth/login", json={"code": "test-login"}, headers={"Origin": "http://localhost"})
            response = client.get("/api/runs", headers={"Origin": "http://localhost"})
        assert response.status_code == 200
        assert response.json() == []
        assert not state_dir.exists()

    # D5 — Details authentication and request-cache contract
    
    Coordinator-confirmed behavior for the bounded event/lineage test task.
    
    - Event and lineage data are keyed by the immutable selected Run ID. Changing the selected Run ID invalidates the previous request generations, aborts outstanding requests, and resets both caches before loading the new run.
    - The first Details visit for a selected run loads events and lineage. Successful event history (`runEventsLoaded`) and lineage (`runLineageRunId`) are reused on repeated Details-tab visits for that same Run ID; toggling between Details, Output, and Terminal must not duplicate those requests.
    - Concurrent duplicate loads are suppressed while each request is busy.
    - The global Refresh button refreshes the process list. There is no separate force-refresh control for historical events or lineage; repeated Details visits remain cache hits. Event pagination is an intentional new request.
    - A 401 is translated by `api()` to the `locked` error and shows the login view. `showLogin()` calls `invalidateSelection()`, which aborts both detail requests and clears both cached Run ID keys. After authentication is restored, reopening Details for the same run must load events and lineage again; cached data must not cross the authentication boundary.
    - A 404/503 error remains an honest visible unavailable state. Repeated tab visits must not fabricate data or create request loops. Existing explicit selection change or authentication reset is the reload boundary; do not invent new retry policy or a new refresh control.
    
    Test with `dashboardHarness()` in `tests/dashboard_test.js`, using deferred responses. The production contract and API are unchanged.

    function updateLifecycleControls(run) {
      const stopBtn = $("#action-stop-btn");
      const killBtn = $("#action-kill-btn");
      const restartBtn = $("#action-restart-btn");
      const duplicateBtn = $("#action-duplicate-btn");
      const pauseBtn = $("#action-pause-btn");
    
      if (!stopBtn || !killBtn || !restartBtn || !duplicateBtn) return;
    
      if (!run || !run.id) {
        stopBtn.disabled = true;
        killBtn.disabled = true;
        restartBtn.disabled = true;
        duplicateBtn.disabled = true;
        if (pauseBtn) {
          pauseBtn.disabled = true;
          pauseBtn.textContent = "Pause";
          pauseBtn.setAttribute("data-action", "pause");
          pauseBtn.className = "lifecycle-btn lifecycle-btn-pause";
          pauseBtn.title = "Pause process";
        }
        return;
      }
    
      const isTerminal = ["finished", "failed", "killed", "lost"].includes(run.status);
      const isInFlight = lifecycleInFlightRunId === run.id;
    
      if (isInFlight) {
        stopBtn.disabled = true;
        killBtn.disabled = true;
        restartBtn.disabled = true;
        duplicateBtn.disabled = true;
        if (pauseBtn) pauseBtn.disabled = true;
        return;
      }
    
      // Stop & Kill
      if (isTerminal) {
        stopBtn.disabled = true;
        stopBtn.title = "Process is already terminated";
        killBtn.disabled = true;
        killBtn.title = "Process is already terminated";
      } else {
        stopBtn.disabled = false;
        stopBtn.title = `Gracefully stop ${run.name || run.command} (${run.id})`;
        killBtn.disabled = false;
        killBtn.title = `Force kill ${run.name || run.command} (${run.id})`;
      }
    
      // Restart: allowed only for terminal processes
      if (isTerminal) {
        restartBtn.disabled = false;
        restartBtn.title = `Restart ${run.name || run.command} as a new process`;
      } else {
        restartBtn.disabled = true;
        restartBtn.title = "Cannot restart an active process. Stop the run first before restarting, or duplicate it.";
      }

    # D5 — Details authentication and request-cache contract
    
    Coordinator-confirmed behavior for the bounded event/lineage test task.
    
    - Event and lineage data are keyed by the immutable selected Run ID. Changing the selected Run ID invalidates the previous request generations, aborts outstanding requests, and resets both caches before loading the new run.
    - The first Details visit for a selected run loads events and lineage. Successful event history (`runEventsLoaded`) and lineage (`runLineageRunId`) are reused on repeated Details-tab visits for that same Run ID; toggling between Details, Output, and Terminal must not duplicate those requests.
    - Concurrent duplicate loads are suppressed while each request is busy.
    - The global Refresh button refreshes the process list. There is no separate force-refresh control for historical events or lineage; repeated Details visits remain cache hits. Event pagination is an intentional new request.
    - A 401 is translated by `api()` to the `locked` error and shows the login view. `showLogin()` calls `invalidateSelection()`, which aborts both detail requests and clears both cached Run ID keys. After authentication is restored, reopening Details for the same run must load events and lineage again; cached data must not cross the authentication boundary.
    - A 404/503 error remains an honest visible unavailable state. Repeated tab visits must not fabricate data or create request loops. Existing explicit selection change or authentication reset is the reload boundary; do not invent new retry policy or a new refresh control.
    
    Test with `dashboardHarness()` in `tests/dashboard_test.js`, using deferred responses. The production contract and API are unchanged.

    ## Filter parameter schema
    
    The endpoint accepts query parameters. `cursor`, `limit`, `sort_by`, and `sort_dir` are already implemented by the frontend. Existing UI filters are partial `name`, `status`, `since`, `until`, `time_field`, `failed_only`, and `lost_only`.
    
    | Query parameter | Accepted value and behavior | Empty/default behavior | UI representation |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `state` | Optional exact enum `active` or `terminal`. `active` covers pending/running/paused; `terminal` covers finished/failed/killed/lost. Anything else raises store `ValueError` and the HTTP route returns 400. | Omit when unset. | Select: Any state / Active / Terminal. Stable ID `history-state-filter` (distinct from the existing status-message element `#history-state`). |
    | `name_exact` | Optional boolean; meaningful with `name`. When true, `name` is case-insensitive equality; otherwise `name` is an escaped case-insensitive substring. | Omit/false when no name is supplied. Never send `name_exact=true` by itself. | Checkbox `history-name-exact` alongside the existing name input. |
    | `exit_code` | Optional integer equality against the stored SQLite INTEGER column. Negative and zero values are valid; do not use truthiness to omit zero. SQLite integer storage is signed 64-bit. | Omit when blank. Reject non-integer and out-of-storage-range input client-side. FastAPI rejects malformed integer query values with 422; validly typed queries reach the store. | Number input `history-exit-code-filter`, integer step; allow signed values. |
    | `restart_of` | Optional string equality against a run's explicit restart-parent Run ID. The store does not infer a relation or resolve a name. | Omit when blank after trimming. | Text input `history-restart-parent-filter`; accept a full explicit Run ID, with no name/command/timestamp inference. |
    | `duplicate_of` | Optional string equality against a run's explicit duplicate-parent Run ID. | Omit when blank after trimming. | Text input `history-duplicate-parent-filter`; accept a full explicit Run ID. |
    | `has_restarts` | Optional boolean. `true` returns runs with at least one direct restart child; `false` means no filter, not “must have no restarts.” | Omit unless checked. There is no API `has_restarts=false` filter. | Checkbox `history-has-restarts`. |
    | `failed_only` / `lost_only` | Existing booleans; backend rejects both true together with HTTP 400. `failed_only` includes status failed or finished with nonzero exit code; `lost_only` means status lost. | Both false unless corresponding preset is active. | Existing mutually exclusive Failures / LOST presets. |
    
    `restart_of` and `duplicate_of` currently have no additional store-level format validation; they are exact string matches. Trim surrounding input whitespace and omit an empty result, but do not infer or rewrite IDs. Do not invent an API filter for “has duplicates.” `include_total` remains false/omitted by default.
    
    ## Canonical filter and preset state
    
    Maintain one canonical object for effective server query values. Preset identity is UI state that must match its effective constraints:
    
    - `recent` clears all filters to defaults. It must not leave either preset boolean set after manual edits or Clear.
    - `completed` sets `status=finished`; that criterion is already visible in the status control.
    - `failures` sets `failed_only=true`, `lost_only=false`; `lost` sets the inverse. These remain visibly active if combined with compatible manual filters such as name/date/exact-name/exit code.
    - If a manual status/state edit conflicts with the active failures/LOST predicate (for example, failures + status=lost, or either preset + state=active), clear that preset boolean and its active button state. Compatible constraints may remain combined while the preset remains visibly active.
    - Applying a manual exact-name or other compatible criterion must not silently clear the active preset. Clearing all filters resets every query field, preset boolean, and active-button indication.
    - The two preset booleans are mutually exclusive. No UI path may send both true.
    - Normalize controls before comparing effective state. A submission that does not change normalized filters should not dispatch another history request.
    - Any effective server filter, sort, or page-size change resets the cursor stack and aborts/ignores older requests. The backend binds a cursor to the complete normalized filter set and sort; a mismatched cursor returns HTTP 400.
    
    Date controls stay as previously implemented; do not change their meaning. Sort values remain `created_at`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `name`, or `numeric_id`, with direction `asc`/`desc`; limit remains 50/100/200 in the UI (API accepts 1–200).
    
    ## Pagination mutation semantics for D4
    
    The backend cursor is keyset pagination and captures an upper `(created_at, id)` boundary on the first page, preventing later/newer inserts from appearing in subsequent pages. It does not provide a full cross-request snapshot: deletes or updates that change filter membership can cause later pages to omit or shift records. D4 must test and document this behavior; it must not assert snapshot isolation.
